preArrival.simple: Check Albania's official visa regime for your passport nationality before booking. Tirana (TIA) is the main air gateway; expect Mediterranean coastal weather, with cooler conditions inland and at altitude.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight & entry planning: Tirana International Airport (TIA) is the main international gateway. Routes and airlines change seasonally; check the airport's current airline list and compare direct flights with connections through nearby European hubs. Ferry services also connect Durrës with Italy; verify schedules with the operator.

Visa & legal compliance: Entry rules depend on passport nationality, purpose, and length of stay. Check Albania's Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs visa regime and any linked application process before departure; do not rely on a blanket visa-free list. Confirm passport validity requirements with the official authority for your case.

Climate & apparel: Conditions vary between the coast, Tirana, and mountainous interior. Check the forecast for each stop and season; pack sun and rain protection for coastal trips and warmer layers for elevation or winter. Use respectful dress at religious sites and follow posted rules.

Checked 2026-11-02; schedules, entry rules, and weather are subject to change.

arrival24h.simple: Albania uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type C and F sockets. TIA's official bus to Tirana is listed as hourly, 24/7, and 400 ALL; licensed airport taxis are available at the terminal.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: Albania uses 230 V at 50 Hz with Type C and F sockets. Check whether your devices support 230 V; a plug adapter does not convert voltage.

Connectivity & payments: Mobile coverage, roaming, eSIM availability, and card acceptance depend on provider and location. Confirm service with your carrier before travel and keep a modest amount of Albanian lek (ALL) available for small purchases or outages.

Airport transfer: Tirana International Airport lists a public bus between the airport and central Tirana every hour, 24 hours a day, for 400 ALL; the airport says the trip takes about 30-40 minutes. Its official taxi page identifies the licensed airport taxi provider and lists an indicative fare of about 2,200 ALL to central Tirana; traffic and fares can change. Use the airport's current directions page to recheck details on arrival.

Checked 2026-11-02; fares and services may change.

mobility.simple: Use current municipal information for Tirana buses and check official intercity listings before travel; routes, operators, and departure points can vary by city.
mobility.detailed:
Tirana and intercity travel: Tirana has municipal bus services. For intercity journeys, Albania's eTransport platform is linked by Tirana International Airport as a listing of official bus lines, stations, and schedules. Confirm the departure terminal, operator, and schedule directly before setting out.

Shared and on-demand transport: Shared minibuses (often called furgons) operate on some routes, but availability and departure practices vary. Agree the destination and fare before boarding. For app-based rides, check current local availability rather than assuming a service operates nationwide.

Walking: Conditions vary by neighborhood and town. Check the route on arrival, allow for uneven or obstructed sidewalks, and use marked crossings while watching traffic.

sources.topic: Official bus lines, stations, and schedules

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery-app coverage and payment options vary by location. Ask your accommodation about local water and pharmacy access; check prescription rules for any medication you bring.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Daily services: Delivery platforms, grocery options, opening hours, and cashless payment acceptance vary across Albania and can change. Check the app in your destination and confirm address and phone-number requirements before relying on delivery.

Health and water: Do not assume tap-water quality is identical across locations or buildings; ask your accommodation or local water provider, and use sealed bottled or appropriately treated water if uncertain. Bring necessary medication in original packaging and verify import and prescription requirements with an official source before travel. For urgent care, ask your accommodation for the nearest currently operating pharmacy or clinic.

Food and drink: Albanian meals commonly include regional dishes such as byrek and tavë kosi. Ask about ingredients and dietary needs directly; menus and availability vary. Service charges and tipping practices are not uniform, so check the bill and use your judgment.

socialCode.simple: Be courteous at religious and heritage sites, ask before photographing people, and follow your host's lead on greetings, footwear, and home-visit customs.
socialCode.detailed:
Being a guest: Customs differ between households and communities. At religious sites, follow posted dress and photography rules. Ask permission before photographing people, private property, or ceremonies. For a home visit, a small food or hospitality gift is a low-risk choice; ask your host about preferences and follow their lead on shoes and greetings.

Public behavior: Use a polite, measured approach in unfamiliar settings. Do not assume that one etiquette rule applies throughout the country; observe local cues and ask respectfully when unsure. This guidance is intentionally limited to practical courtesies rather than broad claims about national character.

preArrival.simple: V.C. Bird (ANU) is the main gateway; compare regional connections via LIAT 20, Caribbean Airlines, and Google Flights/Skyscanner. Check entry requirements by passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: ANU has regional and international links; island hopping may require separate tickets and connections. Compare broadly, then verify route/season with the airline.

Entry: Antigua and Barbuda's visa requirements and permitted stay depend on nationality and route. Check the government's immigration guidance before booking.

Climate and packing: Tropical heat, rainy season, and hurricane season affect flights and ferries. Check weather advisories; pack sun and rain protection.

arrival24h.simple: Antigua uses 230 V / 60 Hz Type A/B sockets; USD is often accepted alongside the East Caribbean dollar. Confirm taxi fare and mobile coverage on arrival.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 60 Hz, Type A and B sockets. Check device voltage; lodging outlets may vary.

Connectivity and money: XCD is local currency; USD acceptance is common in visitor areas but confirm change. Check roaming/SIM options and carry cash for small vendors.

Airport transfer: Use official taxi dispatch/stands at ANU and confirm fare, destination, and luggage before departure. For Barbuda, check current ferry or flight schedules separately.

mobility.simple: Antigua relies on public minibuses, taxis, and rental cars; Barbuda transfers are separate. Check route and return timing before leaving St John's.
mobility.detailed:
On Antigua: Public minibuses run from St John's to villages and beaches, but evening/weekend frequency may be limited. Confirm destination and last return locally.

Between islands: Ferry and small-aircraft schedules connect Barbuda; check operator/weather notices. Rental cars drive on the left and may require a local permit.

Taxis and walking: Agree taxi fare before boarding. Sidewalks may be absent outside town; plan for heat and use safe road shoulders/crossings.

dailyLiving.simple: Restaurant delivery is address-specific and limited outside St John's. Ask accommodation about groceries, drinking water, and pharmacy hours before visiting Barbuda.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Daily services: Call restaurants or ask lodging about current delivery and grocery options; app coverage is not uniform.

Health and water: Follow accommodation/local water guidance and use sealed water if unsure. Bring essential medication; pharmacy stock and late hours are limited on smaller islands.

Money and dining: XCD is standard; USD may be accepted in tourist businesses. Check bills for service and tipping expectations.

socialCode.simple: Use a polite greeting, ask before photographing people, and follow beach, church, and host guidance. Customs differ between Antigua and Barbuda.
socialCode.detailed:
Visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Follow the host's lead.

Public and religious sites: Dress respectfully where requested and ask before photographing people, homes, or ceremonies.

Island etiquette: English is official, with local Creole in daily use. Be courteous and avoid assuming identical customs across islands.

preArrival.simple: AZair for Europe budget flights. Schengen visa: 90/180 rule, passport valid 3+ months. Alpine climate: -2°C to 26°C, cold winters. Smart casual, alpine gear for mountains.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: VIE (Vienna) primary hub. Austrian Airlines (flag carrier). AZair for European budget flights. Direct booking typical. Train network: ÖBB (excellent).

Visa & Legal Compliance: Schengen Area member - 90 days within any 180-day period. Passport valid 3 months beyond departure. Austria-Visa portal for applications.

Climate & Weather: Alpine continental. Vienna: -2°C (Jan) to 26°C (July). Salzburg: -4°C to 25°C. Alps: -10°C to 20°C. Winter skiing Dec-Mar. Pack layers, waterproof jacket, warm clothes for winter.

Apparel Sourcing: Smart casual in cities. Modest dress for religious sites. Alpine/ski gear: Intersport, Hervis (local chains). Size system: European. Dirndl/Lederhosen for festivals (optional).

arrival24h.simple: Power: 230V, 50Hz, Type C/F sockets. Fast 4G/5G, eSIM available. NFC contactless widespread. CAT train to Vienna center.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 230V, 50Hz. Type C (Europlug) and Type F (Schuko) sockets. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-f/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 100+ Mbps. 4G coverage 98%, 5G extensive. ISPs: A1, Magenta Telekom, Drei. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, Holafly. Local SIM: A1 (~€35/week).

Financial Rails: NFC contactless payment ubiquitous. Cash still used in small towns. No mobile money. Tipping: 5-10% (round up).

Airport-to-City: Vienna VIE: CAT (City Airport Train) (€13, 16min) or S-Bahn S7 (€4.20, 25min). Official taxi: ~€50 to center. ÖBB trains to other cities.

mobility.simple: Vienna U-Bahn/S-Bahn/Bahn (extensive). No informal transit. Uber (limited, licensed taxis only). Citybike Wien. Excellent walkability, bike-friendly.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Vienna: U-Bahn (5 lines), S-Bahn, trams, buses. Integrated ticket (Wiener Linien). Salzburg: trolleybuses, buses. ÖBB trains between cities. Apps: WienMobil, Qando.

Informal Transit: Limited. Formal systems dominate. No Matatus/Marshrutka-style informal transit.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Uber restricted (licensed taxis only, no private cars). No Bolt. FreeNow taxi app. Bike-sharing: Citybike Wien (first hour free). E-scooters: Lime, Bird.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Excellent walkability. Dedicated bike lanes. Sidewalks well-maintained. Pedestrian priority at crossings. Very bike-friendly culture.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: Mjam, Wolt, Lieferando. Alcohol: supermarket sales, no restrictions. Pharmacy: many OTC, antibiotics Rx. Tap water safe. Coffee house culture.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: Mjam (Austrian), Wolt, Lieferando. Local: Frichti (meal kits). Grocery delivery: Billa, Spar. Delivery hours limited on Sundays.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, wine shops (Weinhandel). No state monopoly. Drinking age 16 for beer/wine, 18 for spirits. Wine culture (Grüner Veltliner). Tipping expected.

Pharmacy: Many OTC medications. Antibiotics Rx-only. Pharmacies marked with red 'A'. Apotheken (pharmacies) not in supermarkets. 24h pharmacies in cities.

Beverage & Dietary: Tap water potable nationwide, excellent quality (Alpine spring water). Zero-sugar options available. Local: Almdudler, Stroh. Coffee house culture (Viennese coffee). Schnitzel, strudel, Kaiserschmarrn.

Buffet Protocols: Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional: one-plate with refills. Austrian breakfast buffets extensive. No restrictions on refills.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: avoid lilies (death), wine/chocolate OK. Shoes removed in some homes. Dog-friendly (restaurants allowed). Punctuality, formal address, quiet demeanor.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Flowers: odd numbers preferred. Avoid white lilies (death). Wine, chocolate, high-quality items appropriate. Host gifts expected. Unwrap immediately.

Household Norms: Shoes often removed in homes. Follow host's lead. Separate house shoes provided.

Companion Pet Culture: Very dog-friendly. Dogs allowed in restaurants, cafes, public transport. Strict leash laws. Stray dogs rare.

Behavioral Matrix: Individualistic, formality-focused. Formal address (Sie vs. Du). Punctuality essential (5-10 min early is on-time). Indirect communication. Tipping: 5-10% (round up). Personal space respected. Quiet in public. Coffee house culture central to social life. Hofbräu (court brewery) tradition.

preArrival.simple: Nassau (NAS) is the main hub; compare Bahamasair and US/regional connections. Inter-island flights and ferries are separate bookings; check passport-specific entry rules.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: NAS connects many international routes; Grand Bahama (FPO) and Out Islands use smaller airports. Compare broad search and Bahamasair, then verify baggage and island transfer.

Entry: Visa and permitted-stay rules depend on nationality and length/purpose. Check the Bahamas Department of Immigration before booking.

Climate and packing: Tropical heat, hurricane season, and sea conditions affect island schedules. Check National Hurricane Center/local advisories; pack sun and rain protection.

arrival24h.simple: The Bahamas uses 120 V / 60 Hz Type A/B sockets; Bahamian and US dollars trade at par. Confirm island-specific SIM, ATM, and airport taxi options.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 120 V / 60 Hz, Type A and B sockets. Check your device label and adapter.

Connectivity and money: BSD is at par with USD; USD is widely accepted. Card/ATM and mobile coverage vary across Out Islands; carry small cash and check roaming.

Airport transfer: NAS and island airports have separate taxi/shuttle services. Use marked taxi ranks or hotel pickup and agree the fare before departure.

mobility.simple: Nassau uses jitneys and taxis; other islands rely on local taxis, rental cars, and ferries. Confirm route and operating hours—especially the last return trip.
mobility.detailed:
Nassau: Jitneys serve popular routes but do not operate like a fully scheduled metro. Ask locally about route, stop, fare, and last service.

Island links: Bahamas Ferries and domestic flights connect islands; schedules are weather- and season-dependent. Confirm port/airport and luggage allowance.

Taxis and walking: Agree taxi fare in advance. Roads may lack sidewalks; plan for heat, traffic, and limited night lighting.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery services are concentrated in Nassau and some larger islands; verify by address. Ask locally about drinking water and pharmacy access before Out Island travel.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Daily services: Restaurant and grocery delivery are location-specific; call the business or ask lodging for current options and hours.

Water and health: Follow local utility/accommodation advice and use sealed water if unsure. Pharmacy and clinic options are limited on smaller islands; carry essential medicines.

Money and dining: BSD/USD are both used. Check service charge on the bill; tipping customs vary by venue.

socialCode.simple: Ask before photographing people or private property. Follow beach and church guidance; for home visits, ask about footwear and gifts.
socialCode.detailed:
Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small gift is welcome. Follow the host's lead.

Public conduct: English is official. Ask permission before photographing people, homes, or ceremonies and respect posted property rules.

Island differences: Customs and services vary across New Providence, Grand Bahama, and the Out Islands; avoid assuming one island's practice applies everywhere.

preArrival.simple: Grantley Adams (BGI) is Barbados' main gateway; compare Google Flights/Skyscanner with Caribbean Airlines and regional carriers. Check entry requirements for your passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: BGI receives international and regional flights. Compare broad search with Caribbean Airlines/operating carriers and confirm seasonal schedules and baggage.

Entry: Barbados visa requirements, passport validity, and onward-ticket rules depend on nationality. Check Barbados Immigration before booking.

Climate and packing: Tropical climate with rainy/hurricane season risks. Check official weather notices and flight/ferry updates; pack sun/rain protection.

arrival24h.simple: Barbados uses 115 V / 50 Hz Type A/B sockets; local currency is BBD, pegged to USD. Confirm SIM and taxi options at BGI.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 115 V / 50 Hz, Type A and B sockets. Confirm appliance voltage before plugging in.

Connectivity and money: BBD is pegged to USD; USD is widely accepted, but confirm change. Check SIM/roaming availability and card fees.

Airport transfer: BGI has taxi and bus options; check current airport passenger information and confirm taxi fare/destination before departure.

mobility.simple: Barbados has Transport Board buses and privately operated ZR vans/minibuses. Routes and payment differ; ask locally about the last return service.
mobility.detailed:
Public buses: Transport Board buses run on major routes; check current schedules and fares with the operator.

Shared transport: ZR vans and route taxis provide frequent service on some corridors. Confirm destination and fare before boarding; do not assume late-night service.

Taxis and walking: Agree taxi fares before travel. Sidewalks and road shoulders vary; use caution on narrow roads and in rain.

dailyLiving.simple: Food delivery is address-specific; check local restaurant/market services. Follow Barbados Water Authority notices and ask accommodation about pharmacy access.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Restaurant delivery and grocery services vary by parish. Confirm coverage, phone, and payment directly before relying on it.

Water and health: Follow Barbados Water Authority advisories and accommodation guidance. Pharmacies are available in towns; bring prescriptions in original packaging.

Food and payment: BBD/USD are commonly used. Ask about fish and other ingredients/allergens; check bills for service charge and tip at your discretion.

socialCode.simple: Use a polite greeting, ask before photos, and follow church/beach dress guidance. At home, ask about shoes and gifts rather than assuming a custom.
socialCode.detailed:
Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome.

Public settings: English is official. Dress respectfully at churches and ask before photographing people or private property.

Dining: Follow the host's lead and ask about dietary needs. Customs vary by household and parish.

preArrival.simple: Compare only permitted routings with Google Flights or Skyscanner, then confirm each leg with the operating airline. Check Belarus MFA entry rules and your government's current travel advice before booking.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight search and routing: Minsk National Airport (MSQ) is the main international gateway. Google Flights and Skyscanner can compare listed itineraries, but route availability, airspace, payment options, and connections can change. Verify the complete itinerary with carriers and review current travel advice before paying.

Entry rules: Visa eligibility, permitted crossings, and stay conditions depend on passport nationality and route. Check the Belarus MFA visa information; do not rely on a generic visa-free summary.

Climate and packing: Minsk has cold winters and warm summers, with regional variation. Check a current forecast for each stop. Pack insulated layers and winter footwear in cold months, plus rain protection in shoulder seasons.

arrival24h.simple: Minsk uses 220 V / 50 Hz Type C and F sockets. Confirm roaming and card acceptance with your providers; keep a lawful backup payment option.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check device voltage labels; an adapter changes plug shape, not voltage.

Connectivity and money: Roaming, local SIM eligibility, and foreign-card acceptance depend on provider and current restrictions. Ask your carrier and bank before travel; do not rely on a foreign card working everywhere. Use only payment methods permitted for your circumstances.

Airport transfer: Check MSQ's current transport and passenger notices. Use clearly identified licensed services and confirm the destination and fare before leaving the terminal.

mobility.simple: Minsk has metro and surface public transport. Check official route and ticket information; service, taxi apps, and intercity options vary by destination.
mobility.detailed:
Minsk: The metro covers major corridors; buses, trolleybuses, and trams fill out the city network. Check current routes, operating hours, and ticket validation rules with the transport operator before setting out.

Beyond Minsk: Intercity rail and scheduled buses use different stations and operators. Confirm the departure point as well as the timetable. Shared minibuses may serve some corridors, but do not assume a fixed schedule.

Taxis and walking: Use a licensed taxi or a locally available, verified dispatch service; confirm the fare before boarding. Sidewalk and crossing conditions vary by neighborhood, so check the route rather than assuming it is walkable.

dailyLiving.simple: Use BYN for everyday cash needs and confirm foreign-card support before relying on it. Delivery, pharmacy hours, and water advice are location-specific.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Shopping and delivery: App coverage and accepted payment methods vary by address. Check the exact Minsk delivery zone and phone-number requirements in the current app before depending on delivery; smaller cities may have fewer options.

Pharmacy and water: Bring prescription medicines in original packaging and verify import rules. Ask your accommodation about local water quality and use sealed or treated water if unsure. Locate an open pharmacy near your stay rather than assuming 24-hour service.

Food and payment: Belarusian ruble (BYN) is the local currency. Keep an appropriate, lawful backup payment method. Try local dishes such as draniki, and check menus for ingredients and dietary needs. Buffet rules and service charges are venue-specific; check posted terms and the bill.

socialCode.simple: At a home visit, ask whether to remove shoes and what gift is welcome. Use a polite greeting, ask before photographing people, and follow local rules at official sites.
socialCode.detailed:
Home visits: Ask your host about footwear and gift preferences; a small packaged food gift is a low-risk option when appropriate. Do not assume flowers, alcohol, or shoes are welcome in every household.

Communication: Belarusian and Russian are both used; ask which language your counterpart prefers instead of assuming. Start with a courteous, somewhat formal greeting and follow the host's lead.

Photography and conduct: Ask permission before photographing people or private property. Follow posted restrictions at government, transport, and security-sensitive sites. Customs vary by person and setting, so avoid treating one etiquette rule as universal.

preArrival.simple: Philip S. W. Goldson (BZE) is the international gateway; compare Google Flights/Skyscanner and confirm regional connections with the airline. Entry rules depend on passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: BZE serves Belize City; smaller airstrips and domestic flights connect islands and inland destinations. Compare broad flight search, then confirm schedules, baggage, and ground/water transfer with the carrier.

Entry: Check Belize Immigration and the relevant embassy for nationality-specific visa, passport, onward-ticket, and stay requirements. Do not rely on a generic visa-free list.

Climate and packing: Tropical heat, rain, and hurricane season affect coastal/island plans. Check current forecasts and advisories; pack sun and rain protection, light layers, and reef-conscious beach gear.

arrival24h.simple: Belize uses 110 V / 60 Hz Type A/B outlets; Belize dollars are pegged to USD. Check roaming/SIM coverage and arrange your airport or water taxi transfer in advance.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 110 V / 60 Hz, Type A and B sockets. Check device voltage labels; bring a compatible adapter if needed.

Connectivity and money: BZD is pegged at BZ$2 to US$1; US dollars are accepted in many visitor businesses, but confirm change and card fees. Mobile data and card acceptance are less consistent on cayes and in rural areas.

Arrival transfer: Check BZE passenger information and the onward operator if continuing to a caye. Confirm water-taxi terminal, sailing time, luggage rules, and pickup before leaving the airport.

mobility.simple: Intercity buses connect Belize City with towns; cayes rely on water taxis and small aircraft. Confirm the exact terminal and last sailing before planning connections.
mobility.detailed:
Intercity: Scheduled coaches serve major land routes; check current operator times and departure terminals. Rural services may be infrequent.

Islands: Water taxis and domestic flights are the main links to cayes. Use the operator's current timetable and allow buffer for weather or missed connections.

Local trips: Taxis are common; agree the fare before boarding. Walking routes may lack continuous sidewalks, lighting, or shade; plan for heat and rain.

sources.topic: San Pedro Belize Express Water Taxi

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery apps are limited outside Belize City; ask lodging about local groceries, water, and pharmacy access before going to a caye or reserve.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Shopping and delivery: Restaurant delivery and grocery services are location-specific; call or message the business to confirm coverage, hours, and payment.

Water and pharmacy: Use sealed or appropriately treated water unless local guidance confirms otherwise. Pharmacies and clinics are thinner outside towns; bring essential medicines in original packaging.

Food and money: BZD and USD are used in many visitor settings, but verify exchange and change. Ask about ingredients/allergens and check whether service is included.

socialCode.simple: Belize is multilingual and culturally diverse. Ask before photographing people or ceremonies, and follow local and host guidance on beach, village, and heritage-site conduct.
socialCode.detailed:
Language: English is official; Spanish, Kriol, Garifuna, and Mayan languages are also used. Ask which language is preferred rather than assuming.

Visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Follow the host's lead on greetings and shared meals.

Photography and environment: Ask permission before photographing people or private property. Follow reef, wildlife, and archaeological-site rules.

preArrival.simple: Compare Sarajevo and regional-airport routes with Google Flights or Skyscanner; AZair can help find low-cost European connections. Entry rules depend on passport nationality.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Sarajevo (SJJ) is the main gateway; Mostar and Tuzla have smaller, changing route networks. Compare with Google Flights or Skyscanner, and use AZair for low-cost European combinations. Check the operating airline and the full ground transfer before booking.

Visa and entry: Bosnia and Herzegovina is outside Schengen. Entry permission and passport-validity rules depend on nationality and trip details; check the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant embassy before booking.

Climate and clothing: Sarajevo has cold winters and warm summers; Mostar and the Adriatic-influenced south are milder. Check forecasts for each stop, pack layers, and follow posted dress requirements at religious sites.

arrival24h.simple: Sarajevo uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type C and F sockets. Keep some convertible marks (BAM) available and confirm card/roaming support with your providers.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check device voltage labels; a plug adapter does not convert voltage.

Connectivity and payment: Roaming and eSIM options depend on your carrier. Cards are accepted in many urban businesses, but keep BAM cash for small merchants or outages; check foreign-card fees with your bank.

Airport and first transfer: Sarajevo Airport's route and passenger information can change. Check the current airport page on travel day; use marked taxi services or confirm the destination and fare with a verified booking before leaving.

mobility.simple: Sarajevo has trams, trolleybuses, buses, and minibuses; routes and ticket details are operator-specific. Intercity coaches and rail require separate schedule checks.
mobility.detailed:
Sarajevo: GRAS lists tram, trolleybus, bus, and minibus services. Check current notices, route maps, and ticket validity locally; disruptions can change service.

Between cities: Coach and rail options vary by corridor. Confirm the departure station and operator, especially for cross-border journeys. Shared vans may run on some routes but do not assume fixed departure times.

Taxis and walking: Verify app coverage in the city where you are staying. Old-town paving and hilly streets can be uneven; check the route and use marked crossings.

Health and water: Water quality and building plumbing can vary; ask your host or use sealed/treated water if uncertain. Bring prescription medicines in original packaging and verify import rules.

Food and payment: Sarajevo specialties include ćevapi and burek; ask about ingredients and dietary needs. BAM is the local currency. Tipping and service charges vary by venue; review the bill rather than assuming a fixed rate.

Religious and public settings: Dress respectfully where requested, observe posted rules, and ask permission before photographing people, ceremonies, or private property.

Language and etiquette: Bosnian, Croatian, and Serbian are used across the country. Begin politely and follow the other person's preferred language and level of formality; avoid generalizing customs across communities.

preArrival.simple: Compare Google Flights or Skyscanner with Brazil-focused Decolar, then book/check the operating airline. Brazil is large: choose an airport for the actual region you plan to visit.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Brasília (BSB) is a central hub; São Paulo (GRU/CGH), Rio (GIG/SDU), and other regional airports serve different itineraries. Use Google Flights/Skyscanner for broad comparisons and Decolar for Brazil-focused booking; verify baggage, airport, and connection terms with the airline.

Entry rules: Visa and eVisa requirements depend on nationality, passport, purpose, and date. Check Brazil's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and consular guidance before payment; do not infer eligibility from an OTA listing.

Climate and packing: Brazil spans equatorial, tropical, highland, and subtropical climates. Check the weather for each state and season; pack sun/rain protection and light layers.

arrival24h.simple: Brazil uses Type N sockets; voltage is commonly 127 or 220 V at 60 Hz depending on location. PIX is widely used, but visitor access depends on a Brazilian account/provider.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: Type N sockets; 127/220 V at 60 Hz, depending on city and property. Check appliance input labels and the accommodation's local supply. A plug adapter does not convert voltage.

Connectivity and payments: Confirm roaming/eSIM coverage with your carrier. PIX is ubiquitous domestically, but visitors may not be able to register without local banking access; retain an international card and some BRL cash.

Arrival transfer: Airports and city transport differ widely. Check the airport's official ground-transport page, use marked taxi/ride-hailing pickup points, and confirm the fare and destination before leaving.

mobility.simple: Brasília relies on metro and buses; other cities have their own systems. For intercity travel, compare airline routes with bus operators such as ClickBus.
mobility.detailed:
Brasília: Metro-DF and city buses connect major districts; confirm route, hours, and ticket options with the operator. Distances and superblocks make some journeys longer on foot than the map suggests.

Other cities and long-distance travel: São Paulo, Rio, and other capitals have distinct metro/BRT systems. Compare flights with coach routes and current bus operators; confirm the departure terminal and baggage rules.

Ride-hailing: Uber and 99 are common in many urban areas, but coverage varies. Check the registered plate and pickup point in-app; use marked crossings and account for heat and uneven sidewalks.

dailyLiving.simple: iFood and Rappi cover many urban addresses; check the exact zone. PIX, tap water, pharmacies, and comida por quilo practices vary by location and venue.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery and shopping: iFood and Rappi are widely used in larger cities; enter the exact address and check phone/payment requirements. Mercado Livre is a major marketplace, but delivery times depend on region.

Food and payment: PIX is a domestic instant-payment rail; use only a payment method you can lawfully register. Comida por quilo restaurants charge by weight; check how tare is handled and the posted price per kilogram.

Health and water: Tap-water quality and infrastructure vary by municipality/building. Ask locally and use sealed or treated water if uncertain. Bring prescriptions in original packaging and verify import rules.

socialCode.simple: Portuguese is the national language. Ask before photographing people; follow local cues on greetings, footwear, religious sites, and shared dining.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings and language: Brazilian Portuguese is used nationwide, with regional variation. A friendly greeting is common, but physical contact preferences differ; follow the other person's lead.

Home and dining: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether to bring something for the host. At shared meals, ask about dietary needs and follow the host's serving style.

Photography: Ask permission before photographing people, homes, or ceremonies. Follow posted rules at religious and heritage sites; avoid broad claims about one national etiquette.

Flight routing: Sofia (SOF) is the main hub; Varna (VAR) and Burgas (BOJ) serve Black Sea destinations. Compare Google Flights/Skyscanner with AZair for low-cost European itineraries, then confirm baggage and route with the airline.

Entry rules: Bulgaria is in Schengen. Visa requirements depend on nationality and prior Schengen stays; check the European Commission's current short-stay rules and the relevant consulate.

Climate and clothing: Sofia has cold winters and hot summers; the Black Sea coast and mountain areas differ. Check the forecast for each stop and pack layers, rain protection, or beach gear as appropriate.

arrival24h.simple: Bulgaria uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type C and F sockets. The currency is now the euro; Sofia Airport has current metro, bus, and official taxi guidance.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check your device label; an adapter changes plug shape but does not convert voltage.

Connectivity and money: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026; euro banknotes and coins are now the sole legal tender. Cards and contactless payment are common in cities, but keep a small backup and check your bank's fees.

Airport transfer: Sofia Airport publishes current metro, bus, terminal-transfer, and taxi information. Check first/last departures and service changes on arrival day; use the airport-recommended taxi stand or dispatch office.

mobility.simple: Sofia has metro, trams, buses, and trolleybuses. Use Sofia Traffic's live route changes and ticket guidance; city and intercity fares are separate.
mobility.detailed:
Sofia: Metro, trams, buses, and trolleybuses serve the city. Sofia Traffic provides route changes, stops, and the Sofia2Go journey tools; check ticket validity and current service notices before boarding.

Beyond Sofia: Varna, Plovdiv, and other cities operate their own networks. Bulgarian State Railways (BDZ) serves intercity rail; confirm station, schedule, and ticket details for the chosen route.

Ride-hailing and walking: Bolt availability varies by city. Old-town paving, hills, and winter conditions can affect walking; inspect your route and use marked crossings.

dailyLiving.simple: Glovo and eBag serve parts of the larger cities; check exact-address coverage. Bulgaria now uses euros, and water or pharmacy guidance should be checked locally.

Pharmacy and water: Ask your accommodation about the nearest open pharmacy and local water notices. Carry prescriptions in original packaging and verify medicine import rules before travel.

Food and payment: Try shopska salad, banitsa, or regional dishes; confirm ingredients and dietary needs. Euro is the currency. Service charges and tipping vary by venue; review the bill.

socialCode.simple: Ask before photographing people or religious services, and follow site dress rules. At a home visit, ask about shoes and gifts rather than relying on folk generalizations.

Visits and gifts: Household preferences vary. Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Do not rely on the often-repeated head-nodding generalization; confirm meaning if a gesture matters.

Religious sites: Follow posted rules on clothing, photography, and services. Ask permission before photographing people or private property.

Conversation: Bulgarian is the official language; English use varies by age and location. Start courteously and ask which language is comfortable.

preArrival.simple: Compare Praia and island gateways with Google Flights/Skyscanner, TAP, and Cabo Verde Airlines; domestic island links are separate. Check the consular portal for visa and pre-registration requirements.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Praia (RAI), Sal (SID), and Boa Vista (BVC) serve different islands. Compare Google Flights/Skyscanner with TAP and Cabo Verde Airlines; inter-island flights and ferries require separate planning.

Entry: Visa exemptions, visa requirements, and pre-registration/TSA procedures depend on nationality and visit. Check Cabo Verde's official Consular Portal before booking and complete any required pre-registration.

Climate and packing: Dry, sunny conditions are common, but wind, dust, and island microclimates vary. Check forecasts; pack sun protection, light layers, and sturdy footwear for volcanic terrain.

sources.topic: Cabo Verde Consular Portal: visas and entry pre-registration

arrival24h.simple: Cabo Verde uses 220 V / 50 Hz Type C and F sockets. Escudo is pegged to the euro; keep cash for smaller islands and check roaming coverage.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Confirm your device input and adapter compatibility.

Connectivity and payments: The Cabo Verde escudo (CVE) is pegged to the euro; cash and card acceptance varies by island and merchant. Check roaming/SIM options and carry cash for outages or small businesses.

Airport transfer: Airports and ground transport differ by island. Check ASA's current passenger information and arrange licensed taxi or hotel transfer; confirm fare and pickup before leaving.

mobility.simple: Inter-island travel uses domestic flights and ferries; CV Interilhas publishes sailing information. On-island transport often relies on shared aluguer minibuses and taxis.
mobility.detailed:
Between islands: Compare domestic flights with CV Interilhas ferries. Schedules are weather-sensitive and can change; confirm departure port, check-in time, and current notices.

On-island: Aluguer shared minibuses and taxis serve many routes, but frequencies vary. Confirm destination and fare before boarding; some routes depart when full.

Walking: Terrain can be steep, rocky, and exposed to sun/wind. Plan water, footwear, and return transport, especially outside town centres.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery and online retail are limited outside Praia and larger island towns. Confirm water, pharmacy, and shop hours with your accommodation before remote trips.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Daily services: App-based delivery is limited and island-specific. Ask your accommodation about local shops, phone coverage, and opening hours; plan supplies before moving to smaller islands.

Health and water: Use sealed or treated water unless local providers confirm otherwise. Pharmacy stock and hours vary; carry essential medicine in original packaging and verify import rules.

Food and payment: Seafood, cachupa, and local produce vary by island. Ask about ingredients and dietary needs. CVE cash is useful; check any card surcharge and restaurant service charge.

socialCode.simple: Portuguese and Cape Verdean Creole are used; ask which language is preferred. Ask before photographing people and follow host cues on greetings and gifts.
socialCode.detailed:
Language and greetings: Portuguese is official and Cape Verdean Creole is widely spoken. Ask which language your host prefers and greet people politely.

Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Customs differ between islands and households.

Photography and environment: Ask permission before photographing people or private property. Follow local guidance on beaches, trails, and protected areas.

preArrival.simple: Use Google Flights/Skyscanner and AirAsia MOVE/Traveloka for Southeast Asian connections, then verify routes. Cambodia's official e-Visa is nationality- and checkpoint-dependent.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Phnom Penh's new Techo International Airport (KTI) is the capital gateway; Siem Reap-Angkor (SAI) serves temple-region trips. Airport and airline routes change, so confirm airport code, ground transfer, and itinerary with the carrier.

Entry: Cambodia's e-Visa, visa-on-arrival, and pre-arrival registration rules depend on nationality and entry point. Check the official eVisa portal and current immigration notices; use only official portals.

Climate and packing: Tropical wet/dry seasons bring heat, humidity, and heavy rain. Check forecasts and flood advisories; pack sun/rain protection and modest clothing for temples.

arrival24h.simple: Cambodia uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type A, C, and G outlets. Riel and US dollars are both encountered; confirm ATM fees and carry small-denomination cash.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz; Type A, C, and G sockets are reported. Check the lodging outlet and device voltage before use.

Connectivity and money: Local SIMs are available from Cambodian operators; check registration and coverage. Riel (KHR) is the currency; US dollar cash is also used in many visitor transactions. Use clean small notes and confirm current acceptance.

Airport transfer: Phnom Penh KTI and Siem Reap SAI are separate airports; confirm the airport code and current official ground transport before booking onward travel. Use official taxi/app pickup areas and agree the fare.

mobility.simple: Phnom Penh and Siem Reap rely on buses, tuk-tuks, and app-booked rides. Grab and PassApp coverage is city-specific; confirm price and destination in-app.
mobility.detailed:
City trips: Local buses serve selected Phnom Penh corridors; tuk-tuks and remorks fill many gaps. Grab and PassApp are common booking options in larger cities; verify the vehicle and displayed fare.

Intercity: Coaches connect Phnom Penh, Siem Reap, Battambang, and border towns. Check operator, station, and arrival point; road times vary substantially.

Walking and temples: Heat, traffic, and sidewalk gaps make walking tiring. At Angkor and other heritage areas, use designated paths, heed conservation notices, and plan transport between sites.

dailyLiving.simple: Nham24 and GrabFood serve parts of the larger cities; check address coverage. Use sealed water and verify pharmacy availability before rural or island trips.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Nham24 and GrabFood are options in Phnom Penh and other covered cities; enter the exact address and verify hours and payment methods. Service is limited in smaller towns.

Health and water: Use sealed bottled or properly treated water. Pharmacies vary in stock and opening hours; bring essential medication in original packaging and check import rules.

Payment and food: Cash remains useful; ABA and Wing wallets are locally important but visitor access varies. Ask about ingredients, allergens, and spice. Buffet terms are venue-specific.

socialCode.simple: At pagodas and temples, cover shoulders and knees and remove shoes where directed. Ask before photographing people or religious spaces.
socialCode.detailed:
Temples: Follow posted clothing and photography rules, remove shoes where instructed, and avoid touching sacred objects or climbing on monuments.

Home visits and dining: Ask about shoes and gifts; observe the host's lead on shared dishes. Ask about dietary needs and use serving utensils where provided.

Interactions: Khmer is the national language. A polite greeting and asking permission before photography are good defaults; customs vary by household and community.

preArrival.simple: Compare Google Flights/Skyscanner with Chinese carrier sites; domestic routes are often best checked with Air China, China Eastern, or China Southern. Visa/transit eligibility is nationality- and city-specific.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Beijing (PEK/PKX), Shanghai (PVG/SHA), and Guangzhou (CAN) are major gateways. Compare international options broadly, then check Chinese carriers directly for domestic connections and baggage.

Entry: Visa-free and transit policies vary by nationality, itinerary, port, and date. Check China's National Immigration Administration and the relevant embassy; confirm transit eligibility before buying a non-refundable ticket.

Climate and packing: China spans multiple climate zones. Check city/season forecasts and air-quality alerts; pack region-appropriate layers and modest clothing for religious/heritage sites.

arrival24h.simple: China uses 220 V / 50 Hz Type A, C, and I sockets. Prepare AliPay/WeChat Pay setup, local data access, and cash before relying on apps at arrival.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 50 Hz, Types A, C, and I. Check your device label; plug adapters do not convert voltage.

Connectivity and payments: Google services and some international apps may be restricted. Set up lawful connectivity/payment options before arrival. Alipay and WeChat Pay support foreign visitors in some cases, but card linking/verification can fail; retain CNY cash.

Airport transfer: Beijing, Shanghai, and other airports have separate rail, metro, taxi, and bus connections. Confirm the airport terminal and official pickup zone; use authorized taxis or verified apps.

mobility.simple: Major Chinese cities have extensive metro and bus networks; Didi and bike-share are app-based. Use local transit apps and verify payment setup before traveling.
mobility.detailed:
Urban transit: Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and other large cities operate metro/bus networks with city-specific cards and apps. Check route maps, service alerts, and ticket rules; English support varies.

Intercity: China Railway 12306 is the official rail booking channel; passport details must match the ticket. Book early for peak periods and confirm station names, which can differ within a city.

Ride-hailing and micro-mobility: Didi and shared bikes are common where available, typically requiring app/payment setup. Sidewalks may be crowded with e-bikes; use marked crossings and follow local traffic flow.

dailyLiving.simple: Meituan and Ele.me are major food-delivery apps, but require app/payment/address setup. Do not drink untreated tap water; pharmacy rules and availability vary.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery and shopping: Meituan and Ele.me are common city food-delivery platforms; local phone, address format, language, and payment setup may be required. Confirm that your account works before depending on delivery.

Health and water: Tap water is generally not consumed untreated. Use boiled or sealed water. Bring prescription medicines in original packaging and check import restrictions; use major-chain pharmacies for routine items.

Food and daily payment: Alipay/WeChat Pay dominate many transactions, but visitors should keep cash and a working backup. Ask about ingredients and allergens; buffet policies are venue-specific.

socialCode.simple: At temples, follow posted dress rules and avoid placing chopsticks upright in rice. Ask before photos; customs vary by region and household.
socialCode.detailed:
Visits and gifts: Ask whether a small gift is welcome and follow the host's lead on presentation. Avoid assuming one gift taboo applies to every family or region.

Dining: Shared dishes and chopsticks are common. Do not stick chopsticks vertically into rice; ask about dietary needs and use serving utensils when offered.

Public conduct: Ask permission before photographing people, homes, and ceremonies. Follow posted restrictions at government, transport, and security-sensitive locations.

preArrival.simple: Compare SJO and LIR gateways with Google Flights/Skyscanner; include long ground transfers in the fare calculation. Check Costa Rica's entry rules and current health advisories.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Juan Santamaría (SJO) serves the Central Valley; Liberia (LIR) is convenient for Guanacaste. Compare flights with ground time and seasonal route availability included.

Entry: Costa Rica's Immigration Directorate publishes visa requirements by nationality. Check passport validity, onward-ticket, and permitted-stay rules for your case before travel.

Climate and packing: Pacific, Caribbean, and highland weather differ; rainy-season timing is regional. Check forecasts, road conditions, and park advisories; pack rain protection and trail footwear.

arrival24h.simple: Costa Rica uses 120 V / 60 Hz Type A/B outlets; colón is the currency, though USD is accepted in many tourist areas. Check SIM coverage and airport bus/taxi options.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 120 V / 60 Hz, Type A and B sockets. Check device labels before plugging in.

Connectivity and money: Buy a local SIM from a recognized carrier or confirm roaming. Cards are common in cities; CRC cash is useful, and USD acceptance/exchange varies by business.

Airport transfer: SJO and LIR have different bus, shuttle, and taxi arrangements. Check the airport's current passenger page and use official taxi ranks or licensed shuttles; confirm destination and price.

mobility.simple: San José has bus and commuter-rail options; intercity travel is mostly by coach. Uber availability varies by city and legal status; confirm each route and pickup.
mobility.detailed:
San José: Buses and commuter rail serve parts of the metro area; check current routes, operating days, and payment directly with the operator.

Intercity: Coaches are the main public link between regions. Confirm terminal, operator, luggage policy, and return schedule; some beach routes fill quickly in peak season.

Ride-hailing and walking: Uber and local taxi services vary in coverage and regulation. Use marked crossings; sidewalks and road shoulders can be inconsistent outside central areas.

sources.topic: Costa Rica Tourism Board transport information

dailyLiving.simple: Uber Eats and local delivery cover parts of San José and tourist towns; verify the address. Ask accommodation about local water advisories and pharmacy hours.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Uber Eats and local services are address-specific; check phone, payment, and hours in-app. Remote beaches and rural lodges may have no delivery.

Water and health: Tap water is treated in many urban areas, but supply and advisories vary by region/building. Ask locally; use sealed or treated water if unsure. Carry prescriptions in original packaging.

Food and payments: CRC is accepted everywhere; USD may be accepted in tourist districts but change may be in colones. Ask about ingredients and check service charges before tipping.

socialCode.simple: Use a polite greeting, ask before photographing people, and follow host cues on footwear and meals. At parks, follow wildlife and conservation rules.
socialCode.detailed:
Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small local-food gift is welcome. Household customs vary.

Conversation: Spanish is the official language; English is common in some tourism areas but not universal. Ask which language is comfortable.

Outdoor conduct: Follow park rules, stay on marked trails, and do not feed wildlife. Ask permission before photographing people or private property.

sources.topic: Costa Rica Tourism Board visitor guidance

preArrival.simple: Compare Zagreb, Split, Dubrovnik, and seasonal coastal routes with Google Flights/Skyscanner; use AZair for low-cost European legs. Check Schengen eligibility and ferry connections separately.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Zagreb (ZAG), Split (SPU), and Dubrovnik (DBV) are major gateways; coastal schedules vary by season. Use Google Flights or Skyscanner for broad comparisons and AZair for low-cost European combinations, then verify the itinerary with the airline.

Entry rules: Croatia is in Schengen. Visa requirements and the 90/180 short-stay limit depend on nationality and time already spent in the area; check current European Commission guidance.

Climate and clothing: Inland Zagreb has colder winters than the Adriatic coast. Summer coastal heat and shoulder-season rain are both possible. Pack layers and sturdy shoes for historic stone streets.

arrival24h.simple: Croatia uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type C and F sockets and the euro. Check each airport's current bus/taxi options and ferry schedules before departure.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check device compatibility; a plug adapter does not convert voltage.

Connectivity and payment: Euro is the currency. Cards and contactless payment are common in cities, but small businesses and islands can differ. Check roaming/eSIM terms and keep some cash for contingencies.

Airport transfer: Zagreb, Split, and Dubrovnik have different bus and taxi arrangements. Check the relevant airport's current passenger page, terminal stop, and operating hours. For island onward travel, use Jadrolinija's current sailing schedule and traffic notices.

mobility.simple: Zagreb has trams and buses; coastal cities rely more on buses and ferries. ZET and Jadrolinija publish routes, tickets, and live service notices.
mobility.detailed:
Zagreb: ZET operates trams and buses and provides a journey planner, timetables, fares, and service updates. Check current line notices and ticket validation rules.

Coast and islands: Local buses and ferries are key links. Jadrolinija's schedule and traffic-status pages are the references for ferry routes; seasonal timetables and reservations differ by line.

Ride-hailing and walking: Check Uber/Bolt availability at the exact location rather than assuming national coverage. Historic centres can have steep, polished stone streets; allow extra time and use marked crossings.

sources.topic: ZET Zagreb route planner, fares, and notices

dailyLiving.simple: Wolt and Glovo are available in parts of Croatia; enter the exact address to confirm coverage. Tap-water and pharmacy advice can vary on islands and in older buildings.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Check Wolt or Glovo for your precise address, phone, and payment method. Island and rural coverage is limited; shops may close earlier outside peak season.

Health and water: Municipal tap water is commonly treated, but ask locally about the building and any advisories. Bring prescriptions in original packaging and locate the on-duty pharmacy for the town you are visiting.

Food and payment: Try regional seafood, olive oil, or dishes such as pašticada; ask about ingredients and allergens. Check the bill for service charges; tipping is discretionary and venue-dependent.

socialCode.simple: At churches, follow posted dress and photography rules. In homes, ask about shoes; in cafés, check the bill and follow the venue's service-charge policy.
socialCode.detailed:
Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small local-food gift is welcome. Customs differ between households and regions.

Religious and heritage sites: Follow clothing and photography rules. Ask before photographing people, ceremonies, or private property.

Public etiquette: Coffee and café time are common social settings, but don't infer a fixed schedule or tipping rule. Review the bill, and follow the host's lead on greetings and formality.

preArrival.simple: Havana (HAV) is the main gateway, but routes and payment options change. Check current government travel advice, Cuban entry rules, and airline requirements before purchase.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: HAV and resort airports serve different itineraries. Verify routes directly with carriers and check current operating/payment conditions; broad search results may not reflect ticket availability.

Entry: Cuba's eVisa/tourist-card and health/arrival requirements depend on nationality, departure point, and purpose. Check official Cuban consular guidance and airline documentation rules before travel.

Climate and packing: Tropical heat and hurricane-season disruption are possible. Check forecasts and advisories; bring prescriptions and essentials because local availability can be inconsistent.

arrival24h.simple: Cuba uses 110/220 V and Type A/B/C/L sockets depending on building. Bring cash in an accepted currency and verify current card, SIM, and airport-transfer options.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: Supply may be 110 or 220 V and sockets vary; check the lodging and device label before use. Bring a voltage converter if the device requires it.

Connectivity and money: Internet/SIM access and international-card acceptance can be constrained and change. Check your bank and carrier before travel and bring sufficient legal cash; exchange only through authorized channels.

Airport transfer: Confirm your airport terminal and pre-book a recognized taxi or accommodation transfer. Availability and payment methods may differ from typical app-based travel.

mobility.simple: Intercity Viazul coaches and domestic flights are limited and should be booked/confirmed early. City transport includes official taxis and shared options; verify availability locally.
mobility.detailed:
Intercity: Viazul coaches and domestic flights connect key visitor destinations; check current schedule, payment, and ticket availability before building tight connections.

City trips: Official taxis, private taxis, and shared vehicles operate differently by city. Agree price, currency, route, and pickup before boarding.

Walking: Pavements, lighting, and service interruptions vary. Carry offline addresses and allow extra time; follow current local notices and government travel advice.

dailyLiving.simple: Online delivery and grocery availability are limited and payment-sensitive. Carry essential medicine and ask accommodation about water and current local supply conditions.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Daily services: Do not assume international food-delivery or online-shopping apps work. Ask lodging or a trusted local contact about current restaurants, shops, and payment methods.

Health and water: Use sealed water unless local guidance confirms otherwise. Bring essential medicines and prescriptions; pharmacy availability can be limited.

Money and dining: Payment options and currency acceptance can change. Confirm the amount/currency before ordering and check current official travel guidance.

socialCode.simple: Ask before photography, especially of officials or security facilities. Use a polite greeting and follow host instructions; customs and services can vary by locality.
socialCode.detailed:
Visits and conversation: A friendly greeting is common; ask before photographing people or homes. Follow the host's lead on footwear and gifts.

Public sites: Respect posted restrictions at government, transport, and security-sensitive locations. Avoid photographing facilities where prohibited.

Dining and gifts: Ask about preferences and dietary needs rather than assuming alcohol, flowers, or a particular gift is suitable.

preArrival.simple: AZair for Europe budget flights. Schengen visa: 90/180 rule, passport valid 3+ months. Continental climate: -3°C to 24°C. Smart casual, beer culture.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: PRG (Prague) primary hub. Czech Airlines (flag carrier). AZair for European budget flights. Direct booking typical. Train network: České dráhy (excellent).

Visa & Legal Compliance: Schengen Area member - 90 days within any 180-day period. Passport valid 3 months beyond departure. Czech-Visa portal for applications.

Climate & Weather: Continental. Prague: -3°C (Jan) to 24°C (July). Brno: -2°C to 25°C. Cold winters, warm summers. Pack layers, waterproof jacket. Snow in winter.

Apparel Sourcing: Smart casual in cities. Modest dress for religious sites. Size system: European. Outdoor gear: Husky (Czech brand). Pivo (beer) culture integral.

arrival24h.simple: Power: 230V, 50Hz, Type C/E sockets. Fast 4G/5G, eSIM available. NFC contactless widespread. Airport Express bus to Prague.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 230V, 50Hz. Type C (Europlug) and Type E (French with male pin) sockets. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-e/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 100+ Mbps. 4G coverage 98%, 5G extensive. ISPs: T-Mobile CZ, O2, Vodafone. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, Holafly. Local SIM: T-Mobile (~€35/week).

Financial Rails: NFC contactless payment ubiquitous. Cash still used in small towns. No mobile money. Tipping: 10% (round up).

Airport-to-City: Prague PRG: Airport Express bus (Kč32, 35min) or public bus (Kč32, 45min). Official taxi: fixed rate (~Kč600-700 to center). Liftago ride-hailing.

mobility.simple: Prague Metro (3 lines), trams, buses. No informal transit. Liftago ride-hailing. Rekola bike share. Excellent walkability, cobblestones.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Prague: Metro (3 lines), trams, buses. Integrated ticket (PID). Brno: trams, buses. České dráhy trains between cities. Apps: PID Lítačka, Liftago.

Informal Transit: Limited. Formal systems dominate. No Matatus/Marshrutka-style informal transit.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Liftago (Czech ride-hailing). No Uber. No Bolt. Bike-sharing: Rekola (Prague), Nextbike (other cities). E-scooters: Lime, Beejump.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Excellent walkability in historic centers. Cobblestones in old Prague - wear comfortable shoes. Sidewalks well-maintained. Pedestrian crossings respected. Beer garden culture.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: DámeJídlo, Wolt, Uber Eats. Alcohol: supermarket sales, no restrictions. Pharmacy: many OTC, antibiotics Rx. Tap water safe. Beer culture.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: DámeJídlo (Czech), Wolt, Uber Eats. Local: Rohlík (grocery). Grocery delivery: Albert, Tesco. Delivery hours limited on Sundays.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, hospody (pubs). No state monopoly. Drinking age 18. Pilsner Urquell, Budějovický Budvar beer culture. Tipping expected.

Pharmacy: Many OTC medications. Antibiotics Rx-only. Pharmacies marked with green cross. Lékárna (pharmacy) not in supermarkets. 24h pharmacies in cities.

Beverage & Dietary: Tap water potable nationwide, excellent quality. Zero-sugar options available. Local: Pilsner beer, Kofola (Czech cola). Czech cuisine: svíčková (beef), goulash, dumplings. Beer cheaper than water.

Buffet Protocols: Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional: one-plate with refills. Czech breakfast buffets. No restrictions on refills.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: avoid lilies (death), beer/food OK. Shoes removed in some homes. Dog-friendly (pubs allowed). Beer culture, direct communication, reserved demeanor.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Flowers: odd numbers preferred. Avoid white lilies (death). Beer, local food, sweets appropriate. Host gifts expected. Unwrap immediately.

Household Norms: Shoes often removed in homes. Follow host's lead. Separate house shoes provided.

Companion Pet Culture: Very dog-friendly. Dogs allowed in pubs, restaurants (patios), public transport. Stray dogs rare. Cat culture present.

Behavioral Matrix: Individualistic, beer-culture-focused. Pivo (beer) central to social life. Punctuality: 5-10 min grace socially. Tipping: 10% (round up). Personal space respected. Reserved initially, warm after first beer. Direct communication. Hobbies: hiking, skiing.

preArrival.simple: Douglas-Charles (DOM) and Canefield (DCF) serve different flights; compare regional airlines and ferry combinations. Check Dominica entry rules by passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: DOM is the main international gateway; DCF serves limited regional flights. Island hopping may be faster by ferry depending on schedule and sea conditions.

Entry: Visa requirements depend on nationality, purpose, and length of stay. Check Dominica Immigration or the relevant embassy before booking.

Climate and packing: Rainforest terrain means frequent showers and humid conditions. Check storm advisories; pack waterproof layers and hiking footwear.

arrival24h.simple: Dominica uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type D/G sockets and East Caribbean dollars. Confirm airport transfer, SIM coverage, and ferry timetable before arrival.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type D and G sockets. Check device labels and bring compatible adapters.

Connectivity and money: XCD is the local currency. Mobile coverage and card acceptance vary outside Roseau; carry cash and check roaming.

Arrival: Check DOM/DCF airport passenger details and arrange taxi or lodging pickup. Ferry terminals are separate; verify sailing schedules and port locations.

mobility.simple: Dominica relies on minibuses, taxis, and ferries; routes are limited outside Roseau. Confirm return service before hiking or visiting remote attractions.
mobility.detailed:
Buses: Privately operated minibuses serve major routes from Roseau, with frequency varying by day and destination. Ask locally for the stop and last return.

Island links: Ferries connect Dominica with nearby islands; weather can disrupt schedules. Confirm the sailing and port on travel day.

Walking and driving: Mountain roads are winding and sidewalks limited. Use a licensed taxi or experienced driver for remote trailheads; check weather and trail status.

dailyLiving.simple: Food delivery is limited; ask locally. Use treated water where advised and plan pharmacy/food supplies before visiting remote villages or trails.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Daily services: Restaurants and grocery delivery are address-dependent and may require calling directly. Confirm hours and cash/card acceptance.

Health and water: Ask accommodation about local water and the nearest pharmacy. Carry essential medicine; supplies are limited outside Roseau.

Food: Fresh produce and seafood availability varies by season. Ask about ingredients and dietary needs; check service charge before tipping.

socialCode.simple: Ask before photographing people or private property. At home, follow host cues on shoes and gifts; observe conservation rules at rivers and trails.
socialCode.detailed:
Visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Follow the host's lead.

Community and nature: Ask permission before photographing people or community events. Follow local trail, river, and protected-area rules.

Language: English is official and Kwéyòl is also used. A polite greeting and asking which language is preferred are good defaults.

preArrival.simple: Santo Domingo (SDQ) and Punta Cana (PUJ) serve different regions; compare flights with Google Flights/Skyscanner and check Dominican entry/e-ticket requirements.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: SDQ serves the capital; PUJ, STI, and other airports reduce ground travel to resort regions. Compare airport location as well as airfare.

Entry: Visa rules and tourist-card/e-ticket requirements depend on nationality and itinerary. Check Dirección General de Migración and complete official arrival/departure forms as required.

Climate and packing: Tropical heat, hurricane season, and mountain conditions vary by region. Monitor weather advisories and pack sun/rain protection.

arrival24h.simple: Dominican Republic uses 120 V / 60 Hz Type A/B sockets and pesos (DOP). Check SIM coverage, ATM fees, and official airport ride pickup before arrival.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 120 V / 60 Hz, Type A and B sockets. Check device voltage and adapter compatibility.

Connectivity and money: DOP is local currency; USD may be accepted in visitor areas. Check exchange rate, card fees, and local SIM registration; retain small pesos for transport.

Airport transfer: SDQ, PUJ, and STI have separate transport systems. Use airport-authorized taxis or verified app pickup; confirm fare and destination before departure.

mobility.simple: Santo Domingo has Metro, OMSA buses, and shared guaguas; intercity coaches serve major cities. Use current operator information and verify routes outside the capital.
mobility.detailed:
Santo Domingo: Metro de Santo Domingo and OMSA buses serve main corridors. Check current fares, operating times, and service notices.

Shared and intercity: Guaguas and minibuses operate on local routes; confirm destination/fare before boarding. Caribe Tours and other coaches connect major cities; verify terminal and schedule.

Ride-hailing: Uber and local apps operate in major cities. Confirm vehicle and pickup in-app; heat, traffic, and sidewalk gaps affect walking.

dailyLiving.simple: PedidosYa and Uber Eats cover many urban addresses; confirm zone. Use bottled water unless local authorities/accommodation confirm tap-water guidance.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: PedidosYa, Uber Eats, and local grocery services serve some cities; check exact address, phone, and payment in-app.

Water and pharmacy: Use sealed or treated water if unsure. Pharmacies are common in cities but stock varies; bring essential medicines in original packaging and verify import rules.

Payments and food: DOP cash is useful; card acceptance varies by merchant. Ask about ingredients/allergens and check receipts for service charges.

socialCode.simple: Use a courteous greeting, ask before photographing people, and follow host cues on shoes and gifts. Customs vary between city, resort, and rural settings.
socialCode.detailed:
Language and greetings: Spanish is the main language. Begin politely and ask if English or another language is preferred.

Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome; follow the host's lead.

Photography: Ask permission before taking portraits or photographing private property. Follow posted rules at churches and heritage sites.

preArrival.simple: Cairo (CAI) is the main hub; compare EgyptAir and regional carriers with Google Flights/Skyscanner. Check Egypt's official eVisa eligibility and current entry conditions.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Cairo (CAI) is the main international hub; Hurghada, Sharm el-Sheikh, and Luxor serve regional itineraries. Compare broad search and EgyptAir/direct carriers; confirm airport, baggage, and connection details.

Entry: Egypt's eVisa portal is official, but eligibility and visa type depend on nationality and trip. Check visa2egypt.gov.eg and the relevant embassy; do not assume visa-on-arrival is available to every traveler.

Climate and packing: Desert heat, Nile Valley conditions, and coastal weather differ. Check forecasts and heat advisories. Bring sun protection, breathable layers, and modest clothing for religious sites.

arrival24h.simple: Egypt uses 220 V / 50 Hz Type C and F sockets. Keep Egyptian pounds and confirm airport transfer details; SIM, card, and cash access vary by provider and venue.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check device labels and use a compatible adapter.

Connectivity and money: Check roaming and local SIM registration with your carrier/operator. Egyptian pound (EGP) cash is useful for small purchases; card acceptance varies by merchant. Use authorized ATMs and check fees.

Airport transfer: Cairo Airport has multiple terminals and transport options; confirm the terminal, official taxi counter/app pickup zone, and destination. Agree fare or use the app estimate before departure.

mobility.simple: Cairo has metro, buses, and minibuses; Metro tickets and lines are operator-specific. Uber, Careem, and inDrive are common app options; intercity rail requires separate booking.
mobility.detailed:
Cairo: Metro is the most predictable option on served corridors; check current Cairo Metro route, hours, and ticket guidance. Buses and minibuses extend coverage but require local route knowledge.

Ride-hailing: Uber, Careem, and inDrive are available in major cities. Confirm the pickup location, vehicle, and fare in-app; traffic can make journey times highly variable.

Intercity and walking: Egyptian National Railways serves major corridors; verify schedule and station details. Sidewalks, heat, and traffic vary; plan crossings carefully and allow extra time.

dailyLiving.simple: Talabat, Breadfast, and Rabbit are urban service examples; check the exact delivery zone. Use bottled water unless your accommodation gives location-specific guidance.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Talabat, Breadfast, and Rabbit serve some city areas; coverage and payment vary by address. Confirm local phone, building, and delivery instructions in the app.

Health and water: Do not assume tap water is suitable for visitors; use sealed bottled water or suitable treatment. Carry essential medicines in original packaging and verify import rules.

Food and payment: EGP cash remains useful alongside cards and local wallets. Ask about ingredients and dietary needs. Pharmacy hours and duty rotas are local; check nearby options after arrival.

socialCode.simple: Dress modestly at religious sites, remove shoes where directed, and ask before photographing people. Use polite greetings and follow your host's cues.
socialCode.detailed:
Religious and heritage sites: Follow posted clothing, footwear, and photography rules. Ask permission before photographing people, especially at worship sites.

Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Offer or receive items with the host's lead; customs vary.

Public interaction: Greetings and expectations vary by setting. Be courteous, ask about dietary needs, and avoid assuming one social rule applies nationwide.

preArrival.simple: Compare San Salvador (SAL) fares with Google Flights/Skyscanner and include the airport road transfer. Check El Salvador's visa rules and current entry requirements by passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: SAL is the main international airport. Compare route and fare, then confirm with the carrier; factor in the road transfer to San Salvador or the coast.

Entry: Visa and permitted-stay rules depend on nationality and itinerary. Check El Salvador's foreign-ministry or immigration guidance before booking; verify any regional C-4 stay calculation for your route.

Climate and packing: Tropical heat and rainy-season storms affect road travel. Check forecasts and local advisories; bring light rain protection, sun protection, and modest attire for religious sites.

arrival24h.simple: El Salvador uses 120 V / 60 Hz Type A/B sockets and the US dollar. Confirm roaming and ride pickup; keep small USD notes for buses and local purchases.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 120 V / 60 Hz, Type A and B sockets. Check device input and adapter compatibility.

Connectivity and money: USD is the official currency. Card acceptance varies; keep small bills. Check SIM/eSIM availability and coverage with local carriers before relying on data.

Airport transfer: SAL is outside central San Salvador. Use official taxi/shuttle or verified app pickup areas, confirm fare/destination, and check road conditions before an onward drive.

mobility.simple: San Salvador relies mainly on buses and BRT; routes and payment vary. Intercity coaches and ride-hailing are city-specific, so confirm stops and fares locally.
mobility.detailed:
San Salvador: Bus and BRT services cover major corridors. Check current operator/municipal information for routes, stops, operating hours, and fares.

Intercity: Coaches link major towns and tourist routes. Confirm terminal, operator, and schedule before travel; avoid assuming a route operates after dark.

Ride-hailing and walking: Uber and local ride services operate in some urban areas. Verify vehicle/pickup and use marked crossings; sidewalk quality varies.

dailyLiving.simple: PedidosYa and Uber Eats cover some urban addresses; check service zones. USD is used; ask locally about water quality and pharmacy access.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: PedidosYa and Uber Eats are options in selected urban zones; verify address, phone, payment, and hours. Rural and beach coverage is limited.

Health and water: Water supply and treatment differ by locality/building. Ask accommodation and use sealed/treated water if uncertain. Bring necessary medicines and verify import rules.

Food and money: USD is used for daily purchases. Ask about ingredients and dietary needs; check receipts for service charge and tip at your discretion.

socialCode.simple: Use a polite Spanish greeting, ask before photographing people, and follow religious-site dress guidance. At home, ask whether to remove shoes.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings and language: Spanish is the official language. Begin politely and ask if another language is preferred.

Home visits: Ask about footwear and whether a small food gift is welcome. Customs vary by household.

Photography: Ask permission before photographing people, homes, or ceremonies. Follow posted rules at churches, archaeological sites, and government facilities.
