preArrival.simple: AZair for Europe budget flights. Schengen visa: 90/180 rule, passport valid 3+ months. Baltic climate: -6°C to 22°C. Smart casual, digital society.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: TLL (Tallinn) primary hub. Nordica (flag carrier). AZair for European budget flights. Direct booking typical. Train network: Elron.

Visa & Legal Compliance: Schengen Area member - 90 days within any 180-day period. Passport valid 3 months beyond departure. Estonia-Visa portal for applications.

Climate & Weather: Baltic continental. Tallinn: -6°C (Jan) to 22°C (July). Tartu: -7°C to 21°C. Cold winters, mild summers. Pack layers, warm clothes for winter. Digital society (e-Residency).

Apparel Sourcing: Smart casual in cities. Modest dress for religious sites. Size system: European. Outdoor gear: Monton (Estonian brand). Digital culture integral.

arrival24h.simple: Power: 230V, 50Hz, Type C/F sockets. Fast 4G/5G, eSIM available. NFC contactless ubiquitous. Tram/bus to Tallinn center.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 230V, 50Hz. Type C (Europlug) and Type F (Schuko) sockets. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-f/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 100+ Mbps. 4G coverage 99%, 5G extensive. ISPs: Telia EE, Elisa, Tele2. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, Holafly. Local SIM: Telia (~€30/week).

Financial Rails: NFC contactless payment ubiquitous. World's most digital society - everything online. Cash declining but still used. Tipping: 5-10% (round up).

Airport-to-City: Tallinn TLL: Tram 4 (€2, 20min) or bus (€2, 30min) to center. Official taxi: metered (~€15-20 to center). Bolt ride-hailing (Estonian-founded).

mobility.simple: Tallinn trams, buses. No informal transit. Bolt ride-hailing (Estonian-founded). Bolt/Tuul bike share. Excellent walkability, Old Town.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Tallinn: trams, buses (no Metro). Integrated ticket (Ühiskaart). Tartu: buses. Elron trains between cities. Apps: Tallinn public transport, Bolt.

Informal Transit: Limited. Formal systems dominate. No Matatus/Marshrutka-style informal transit.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Bolt dominant (Estonian-founded, global). No Uber. No other ride-hailing. Bike-sharing: Bolt (Tallinn), Tuul (Tartu). E-scooters: Bolt, Tuul.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Excellent walkability. Tallinn Old Town (UNESCO) pedestrian-only. Sidewalks well-maintained. Pedestrian crossings respected. Digital culture: mobile ticketing, parking apps.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: Wolt (Estonian-founded), Bolt Food, Foodpanda. Alcohol: supermarket sales, no restrictions. Pharmacy: many OTC, antibiotics Rx. Tap water safe.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: Wolt (Estonian-founded, global), Bolt Food, Foodpanda. Local: eRaketer (grocery). Grocery delivery: Rimi, Prisma. Delivery hours limited.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, kohvikud (cafes). No state monopoly. Drinking age 18. Vana Tallinn liqueur, beer culture. Tipping minimal.

Pharmacy: Many OTC medications. Antibiotics Rx-only. Pharmacies marked with green cross. Apteek (pharmacy) not in supermarkets. 24h pharmacies in cities.

Beverage & Dietary: Tap water potable nationwide, excellent quality. Zero-sugar options available. Local: Vana Tallinn (herbal liqueur), Kalev chocolate. Estonian cuisine: black bread, herring, kama (grain flour). Digital ordering common.

Buffet Protocols: Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional: one-plate with refills. Estonian breakfast buffets. No restrictions on refills.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: avoid lilies (death), wine/food OK. Shoes removed in homes. Dog-friendly (restaurants). Digital culture, reserved demeanor, sauna.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Flowers: odd numbers preferred. Avoid white lilies (death). Wine, local food, digital gifts appropriate. Host gifts expected. Unwrap immediately.

Household Norms: Shoes removed in homes. Follow host's lead. Separate house shoes provided.

Companion Pet Culture: Dog-friendly. Dogs allowed in restaurants (patios), public transport. Stray dogs rare. Cat culture present.

Behavioral Matrix: Individualistic, digital-culture-focused. World's most digital society. Punctuality: 5-10 min grace socially. Tipping: 5-10% (round up). Personal space respected. Reserved initially, warm in sauna. Direct communication. Sauna culture integral to social life. E-Residency program for digital nomads.

preArrival.simple: Addis Ababa is Ethiopian Airlines' main hub. Compare Google Flights/Skyscanner, then confirm routes directly; use Ethiopia's official eVisa site and watch for lookalike portals.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Addis Ababa (ADD) is the principal international gateway and Ethiopian Airlines' hub; domestic services connect regional centres. Compare broad searches, then verify itinerary and baggage with the carrier.

Entry: Ethiopia offers an official government eVisa for eligible travelers and purposes. Check nationality-specific requirements, entry port, and visa terms at evisa.gov.et; the government warns about fraudulent lookalike sites.

Climate and packing: Addis Ababa's elevation brings cooler evenings; lowlands can be much hotter. Check region-specific forecasts, pack sun protection and layers, and verify seasonal road/park access.

arrival24h.simple: Ethiopia uses 220 V / 50 Hz Type C, E, F, and L sockets. Keep ETB cash; card and mobile-wallet access are more limited outside major hotels/cities.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 50 Hz; Type C, E, F, and L outlets are reported. Confirm outlet type at lodging and check device voltage; use a compatible adapter.

Connectivity and payment: Buy a SIM from an authorized operator and check registration requirements. Telebirr is a domestic wallet; visitors may not be able to register. Carry Ethiopian birr (ETB), especially outside large hotels.

Airport transfer: Bole International Airport is the main entry point. Confirm official transport or hotel pickup in advance, and agree taxi destination/fare before leaving the terminal.

mobility.simple: Addis Ababa has light rail, buses, and minibuses; ride apps such as Ride and Feres are city-specific. Intercity travel is best checked with Ethiopian Airlines or bus operators.
mobility.detailed:
Addis Ababa: Light rail and city buses serve selected corridors; shared minibuses are common but routes and fares may be unfamiliar. Ask locally or use an up-to-date route source before boarding.

Ride services: Ride and Feres are local app examples in Addis Ababa; confirm current availability, language, payment, and pickup location. Service is limited outside urban centres.

Intercity and walking: Domestic flights connect distant regions; road trips can take much longer than map estimates. Check current security, weather, and road advice. Sidewalks and crossings vary.

dailyLiving.simple: Food-delivery and grocery coverage is limited and city-specific. Use sealed or treated water, carry essential medicines, and keep cash for small businesses.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Apps and delivery services have narrower coverage than in many capitals; ask your hotel which service reaches the address. Do not rely on delivery outside Addis Ababa without confirmation.

Health and water: Use sealed bottled or appropriately treated water. Carry essential medication in original packaging and verify import rules; stock and opening hours vary by city.

Food and payment: Injera and shared platters are common, but ask about ingredients and dietary needs. ETB cash remains useful. Tipping and buffet practices depend on the venue.

socialCode.simple: Ask before photographing people, religious services, or government sites. Follow hosts' cues at meals; fasting practices and greetings vary by community.
socialCode.detailed:
Religious and public sites: Follow posted dress and photography restrictions; ask before photographing people, ceremonies, or government facilities.

Home and meals: Ask about footwear and dietary needs. Shared platters are common in some settings; use the serving practice offered by the host.

Language and greetings: Amharic is widely used in Addis Ababa, with many regional languages elsewhere. Begin politely and ask which language is preferred; religious observance varies.

preArrival.simple: Compare Paris and regional gateways with Google Flights/Skyscanner; use AZair for low-cost European connections. Corsica needs a separate flight/ferry plan from mainland France.
preArrival.detailed:
National routing: Paris airports (CDG/ORY) and regional gateways serve different regions. Compare broad search with AZair for low-cost European legs, then verify train/airport transfer and baggage.

Corsica: Ajaccio (AJA), Bastia (BIA), Calvi (CLY), and Figari (FSC) serve different parts of the island. Compare seasonal flights with ferries from mainland ports; account for rental-car/coach access from arrival port.

Entry and climate: France is in Schengen; visa requirements depend on nationality and prior 90/180 days. Climate varies from Alpine to Mediterranean. Check regional weather and ferry/flight disruptions.

arrival24h.simple: France uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type E sockets. Corsica uses the same standard; check airport/ferry transfers for the specific island town.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type E sockets. Check grounded plug compatibility and device labels before use.

Connectivity and payments: Euro and contactless are common, but small venues may differ. Check roaming terms and rural/island coverage with your provider.

Airport transfer: Airport and station links vary by city. For Corsica, confirm ferry terminal/airport and local onward buses or car-rental availability before booking accommodation.

mobility.simple: SNCF connects mainland cities; Corsica has limited rail and seasonal buses. Check SNCF and Chemins de Fer de la Corse separately; car access is useful outside towns.
mobility.detailed:
Mainland: SNCF trains connect major cities; local transit is municipal. Check live timetables, reservation requirements, strikes, and station details before travel.

Corsica: Chemins de Fer de la Corse connects Ajaccio, Corte, and Bastia on a limited network. Bus frequency is lower outside peak season; check the current timetable and return service. A car may be useful for remote coves and villages.

Walking and driving: Historic centres may have restricted zones and cobbled streets. Corsican roads are winding; allow extra time and check seasonal ferry/road notices.

sources.topic: Chemins de Fer de la Corse

dailyLiving.simple: Deliveroo, Uber Eats, and grocery services cover many mainland cities; check exact address. Corsica has thinner, seasonal delivery coverage.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Check Deliveroo/Uber Eats at your precise address; coverage falls in rural areas. In Corsica, plan groceries and pharmacy access before leaving larger towns.

Health and water: Follow municipal advisories and ask your accommodation about local supply/building notices. Pharmacies are marked pharmacie; check the duty-pharmacy listing and carry prescriptions in original packaging.

Food and payment: Try island specialties in Corsica and ask about ingredients/allergens. Euro is used. Service charges are shown on bills; additional tipping is discretionary.

socialCode.simple: Use a polite greeting before requests; at religious sites, follow dress/photo rules. Corsica has distinct local traditions, so ask hosts rather than assuming Parisian customs.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings: A courteous bonjour/bonsoir before asking for help is a useful default. Use formal address in unfamiliar settings, then follow the other person's lead.

Home and religious visits: Ask about footwear and gifts. Follow posted rules at churches, museums, and memorials; ask permission before photographing people.

Corsica: Local language and community customs are distinct from mainland settings. Ask about preferences and respect private property, trails, and heritage sites.

preArrival.simple: AZair for Europe budget flights. Schengen visa: 90/180 rule, passport valid 3+ months. Cool temperate climate: 0°C to 24°C. Casual dress, practical.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: FRA (Frankfurt), MUC (Munich), BER (Berlin) major hubs. Lufthansa (flag carrier), Eurowings. AZair for European budget flights. Direct booking typical.

Visa & Legal Compliance: Schengen Area member - 90 days within any 180-day period. Passport valid 3 months beyond departure. Germany-Visa portal for applications.

Climate & Weather: Temperate continental. Berlin: 0°C (Jan) to 24°C (July). Munich: -2°C to 24°C. Hamburg: 1°C to 22°C. Rain year-round. Pack layers, waterproof jacket. Winter can be harsh in south (Alps).

Apparel Sourcing: Practical, casual style. Business casual in cities. Modest dress for religious sites. Size system: European. Outdoor gear: Jack Wolfskin, Vaude (German brands).

arrival24h.simple: Power: 230V, 50Hz, Type C/F sockets. Fast 4G/5G, eSIM available. NFC contactless widespread. S-Bahn train FRA→city center.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 230V, 50Hz. Type C (Europlug) and Type F (Schuko) sockets. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-f/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 150+ Mbps. 4G coverage 99%, 5G extensive. ISPs: Deutsche Telekom, Vodafone, O2. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, Holafly. Local SIM: Telekom (~€40/week).

Financial Rails: NFC contactless payment ubiquitous (Girocard, credit cards). Cash still used in small towns (Germans prefer cash). No mobile money. PayPal common. Tipping: 5-10% (round up).

Airport-to-City: Frankfurt FRA: S-Bahn S8/S9 (€4.65, 15min) or train (€9.75, 12min). Munich MUC: S-Bahn S1/S8 (€13.40, 45min). Berlin BER: Airport Express (€4.40, 30min) or regional train (€9.80, 20min).

mobility.simple: Extensive U-Bahn/S-Bahn networks. No informal transit. Uber (limited, licensed taxis only). Call a Bike, nextbike. Excellent walkability, bike-friendly.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Berlin: U-Bahn (9 lines), S-Bahn (15 lines), trams, buses. Munich: U-Bahn (8 lines), S-Bahn (8 lines). Integrated tickets (Deutschland-Ticket). Apps: DB Navigator, NVV, BVG.

Informal Transit: Limited. Formal systems dominate. No Matatus/Marshrutka-style informal transit.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Uber restricted (licensed taxis only, no private cars). No Bolt. FreeNow (MyTaxi) taxi app. Bike-sharing: Call a Bike (DB), nextbike, Lime. E-scooters: Tier, Lime, Voi.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Excellent walkability. Dedicated bike lanes (Fahrradwege) everywhere. Sidewalks well-maintained. Pedestrian priority at crossings. Very bike-friendly culture.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: Lieferando, Wolt, Uber Eats. Alcohol: supermarket sales, no restrictions. Pharmacy: many OTC, antibiotics Rx. Tap water safe. Pfand (deposit) on bottles.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: Lieferando (Takeaway.com), Wolt, Uber Eats. Local: Frichti (meal kits). Grocery delivery: Rewe, Edeka. Delivery hours limited on Sundays.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, beverage shops (Getränkemarkt). No state monopoly. Drinking age 16 for beer/wine, 18 for spirits. Beer culture integral. Pfand (deposit) on bottles (€0.25).

Pharmacy: Many OTC medications. Antibiotics Rx-only. Pharmacies marked with red 'A'. Apotheken (pharmacies) not in supermarkets. 24h pharmacies in cities.

Beverage & Dietary: Tap water potable nationwide, excellent quality. Zero-sugar options available. Local: Club-Mate, Spezi. German bread culture. Bakeries ubiquitous.

Buffet Protocols: Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional: one-plate with refills. German breakfast buffets extensive. No restrictions on refills.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: avoid lilies (death), wine/chocolate OK. Shoes removed in some homes. Dog-friendly (restaurants allowed). Punctuality, direct communication, recycling culture.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Flowers: odd numbers preferred. Avoid white lilies (death). Wine, chocolate, high-quality items appropriate. Host gifts expected. Unwrap immediately.

Household Norms: Shoes often removed in homes. Follow host's lead. Separate house shoes (Hausschuhe) often provided.

Companion Pet Culture: Very dog-friendly. Dogs allowed in restaurants, cafes, public transport (muzzled in some cases). Strict leash laws. Stray dogs rare.

Behavioral Matrix: Individualistic, punctuality-focused. Arrive on-time (5-10 min early is punctual). Direct communication valued. Formal vs. informal (Du/Sie) distinction. Tipping: 5-10% (round up). Personal space respected. Recycling mandatory (Pfand system). Quiet hours (Ruhezeit) 10pm-7am, Sundays.

preArrival.simple: Compare Accra (ACC) flights on Google Flights/Skyscanner and confirm with the operating airline. Ghana entry rules are passport-specific; use MFA or official immigration guidance.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Kotoka International Airport (ACC) is the main gateway. Compare broad search, then confirm connections and baggage with the carrier; Africa World Airlines serves some regional routes.

Entry: Visa and yellow-fever documentation requirements depend on nationality, origin, and purpose. Check Ghana's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ghana Immigration before travel; don't rely on generic visa-free summaries.

Climate and packing: Accra is hot and humid; northern regions and rainy seasons differ. Check forecast and health advice, pack breathable clothing and rain protection, and dress respectfully at religious sites.

arrival24h.simple: Ghana uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type D and G sockets. Carry Ghana cedis (GHS); MTN MoMo is common but visitor registration/card acceptance varies.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type D and G sockets. Check device labels and bring a compatible adapter.

Connectivity and payments: Check local SIM registration. MTN MoMo is widely used domestically, but visitors may not be able to open an account; retain GHS cash and a bank card. ATM/card availability varies by town.

Airport transfer: Kotoka Airport lists passenger services and transport information. Use official taxi or verified app pickup and agree the destination/fare before leaving.

mobility.simple: Accra relies on tro-tros, buses, and taxis; routes and stops are informal. Uber, Bolt, and Yango operate in cities; verify pickup, fare, and destination.
mobility.detailed:
Accra: Tro-tros and shared vans serve extensive routes, often departing when full. Ask a local for the correct stop/destination and confirm fare before boarding; intercity coaches use designated terminals.

App rides: Uber, Bolt, and Yango coverage varies by city. Confirm the vehicle and plate in-app and use a clear pickup point.

Walking: Heat, road crossings, and sidewalk gaps can make walking difficult. Plan short routes and use marked crossings; allow extra time for traffic.

dailyLiving.simple: Hubtel and Bolt Food are urban delivery examples; check exact address coverage. Use sealed or treated water and confirm pharmacy hours locally.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Hubtel and Bolt Food serve selected urban zones; verify address, phone, payment, and operating hours. Delivery is limited outside major towns.

Health and water: Use sealed bottled or treated water unless local authorities/accommodation give current guidance. Bring prescriptions in original packaging and check import rules.

Payments and food: GHS cash and mobile money are common; visitor access to MoMo varies. Ask about ingredients and allergens. Check receipts for service charges; tipping is discretionary.

socialCode.simple: Ghana is multilingual and culturally diverse. Ask before photographing people or ceremonies, and follow hosts' cues on greetings, footwear, and dining.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings and language: English is official; local language preferences vary by region and household. Ask which language is comfortable and use a courteous greeting.

Home visits and meals: Ask about footwear and whether a small food gift is welcome. Follow the host's lead on shared dishes and ask about dietary needs.

Photography: Ask permission before photographing people, homes, or ceremonies. Follow posted rules at religious, government, and heritage sites; avoid broad cultural assumptions.

preArrival.simple: Use AZair for low-cost European combinations and compare Google Flights/Skyscanner for wider coverage. Check Schengen entry rules and book island ferries with the operator.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Athens (ATH) is the main hub; Thessaloniki and island airports provide other gateways. Compare Google Flights/Skyscanner with AZair for low-cost European legs. Verify seasonal routes with the airline.

Entry rules: Greece is in Schengen. Visa requirements depend on passport nationality and prior Schengen days; check the European Commission's current rules and the relevant consulate.

Climate and clothing: Athens and islands are hot in summer; northern and mountain areas are cooler. Check forecasts and fire/weather alerts, pack sun protection, and use sturdy footwear on archaeological and island terrain.

arrival24h.simple: Greece uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type C and F sockets and the euro. OASA publishes Athens routes, ticket options, and real-time service alerts.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check device labels and adapters before use.

Connectivity and payments: Euro, cards, and contactless are common in cities; cash remains useful in some island and small-business settings. Verify roaming/eSIM coverage for remote islands with your carrier.

Airport transfer: Athens Airport access options include rail/metro, bus, and taxi; check the airport's current page and first/last departure times. In Athens, use OASA service alerts before relying on a specific bus connection.

sources.topic: OASA route, ticket, and real-time service information

mobility.simple: Athens has metro, bus, tram, and trolleybus services; OASA provides ATH.ENA ticket information and live alerts. Island transport is local and seasonal.
mobility.detailed:
Athens: OASA coordinates public transport information and ATH.ENA ticketing; its site links the telematics app and current announcements. Check service disruptions before airport or port transfers.

Islands: Buses and ferries vary by island and season. Confirm the local timetable and ferry operator, and allow time between the port and airport.

Taxis and walking: Ride apps may dispatch licensed taxis rather than private cars. Confirm the fare and pickup point. Historic areas can be crowded, steep, and uneven; use marked crossings.

dailyLiving.simple: efood and Wolt serve many urban addresses; check island coverage in-app. Tap-water advice differs by island, so ask locally rather than assuming nationwide potability.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: efood and Wolt are common options in larger cities; verify the exact address and opening hours. On islands, delivery and grocery services may be limited or seasonal.

Water and pharmacy: Athens tap water is generally supplied as potable, while island sources vary; follow local advice and use sealed water if unsure. Check the on-duty pharmacy listing for each municipality; carry prescriptions in original packaging.

Food and payment: Try regional dishes and ask about allergens or dietary needs. Euro is the currency. Service charges and tipping vary by establishment; check the receipt.

socialCode.simple: At monasteries and archaeological sites, follow dress and photography notices. For home visits, ask about shoes and gifts; customs vary by household.
socialCode.detailed:
Religious and heritage sites: Some sites require modest clothing or restrict photography. Follow posted rules and staff instructions.

Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. If invited to share food, ask about ingredients and follow the host's lead.

Public interaction: Greetings and meal timing vary by region and context. Be courteous, ask before photographing people, and avoid treating hospitality as a single national rule.

preArrival.simple: Maurice Bishop International (GND) serves Grenada; compare regional flights and ferry links. Entry requirements depend on nationality and stay length.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: GND serves Grenada; Carriacou uses smaller aircraft and ferry connections. Compare regional carriers with broad flight search and include island transfer time.

Entry: Check Grenada Immigration for nationality-specific visa, passport, and onward travel requirements.

Climate and packing: Tropical weather and storm season can disrupt air/ferry travel. Check forecasts and advisories; pack sun/rain protection and hiking shoes.

arrival24h.simple: Grenada uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type G sockets and East Caribbean dollars. Confirm airport taxi, SIM, and inter-island ferry arrangements before landing.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type G sockets. Check device compatibility and adapter.

Connectivity and money: XCD is local currency; card acceptance and mobile coverage vary outside St George's. Keep cash and check roaming.

Airport transfer: Use marked taxi services at GND or arrange hotel pickup. Confirm fare and destination; Carriacou ferry connections depart from a separate port.

mobility.simple: Grenada uses minibuses, taxis, and ferries; there is no extensive rail/metro system. Check route and return timing before leaving St George's.
mobility.detailed:
Minibuses: Shared vans connect St George's with many parishes; ask about route, fare, and last departure locally.

Island links: Ferries serve Carriacou and Petite Martinique; schedules may be affected by weather. Confirm the operator and port before travel.

Taxis and walking: Agree fares before boarding. Roads can be steep and lack sidewalks; use caution and plan for rain/heat.

dailyLiving.simple: App delivery is limited and address-dependent; ask locally. Use accommodation water guidance and plan pharmacy access before hiking or visiting Carriacou.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Daily services: Contact restaurants or ask lodging about current delivery/grocery options; services are concentrated around towns.

Health and water: Follow local water advisories and use sealed water if unsure. Pharmacies and clinics are limited outside populated areas; carry essential medicines.

Food and payment: XCD cash is useful for small purchases. Ask about ingredients and check restaurant bills for service charge.

socialCode.simple: Use a friendly greeting, ask before photos, and follow host cues on footwear and gifts. At beaches and waterfalls, respect posted community and conservation rules.
socialCode.detailed:
Visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome.

Public settings: English is official; local Creole is also used. Ask before photographing people or private property.

Outdoor conduct: Follow trail and marine-protection notices; customs vary between Grenada and its sister islands.

preArrival.simple: Guatemala City (GUA) is the main gateway; compare Google Flights/Skyscanner with regional carriers and include the ground route. Entry rules depend on nationality and the CA-4 itinerary.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: GUA serves Guatemala City; Flores (FRS) can shorten travel to Tikal. Compare international search with direct airlines and domestic operators; factor in road time and season.

Entry: Check Guatemala's immigration authority for nationality-specific visa, passport, and stay rules. The CA-4 arrangement affects stays across Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, and Nicaragua; confirm the current total allowance for your case.

Climate and packing: Highlands, coast, and Petén lowlands differ in temperature and rain. Check forecasts; pack layers, rain protection, sun protection, and modest clothing for religious sites.

arrival24h.simple: Guatemala uses 120 V / 60 Hz Type A/B sockets and the quetzal. Confirm airport transfer, card access, and cash needs before leaving La Aurora Airport.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 120 V / 60 Hz, Type A and B sockets. Check device input before use.

Connectivity and money: GTQ is the local currency; cards are useful in cities, while cash is needed in markets and rural areas. Check ATM fees and local SIM registration.

Airport transfer: La Aurora is in Guatemala City. Use authorized airport taxis/shuttles or a verified ride pickup; confirm destination and fare, and plan road time for traffic.

mobility.simple: Guatemala City has Transmetro and Transurbano; intercity travel uses coaches, shuttles, and local buses. Check current routes and safety guidance before using informal transport.
mobility.detailed:
Guatemala City: Transmetro and Transurbano serve key corridors; check current route maps, fares, and service notices with the municipal operators.

Intercity: Tourist shuttles and scheduled coaches connect Antigua, Lake Atitlán, and other destinations. Confirm pickup point, luggage, and daylight arrival; local buses (camionetas) have different comfort and safety conditions.

Ride-hailing and walking: Uber operates in some cities; coverage varies. Use verified pickups and marked crossings; steep terrain and uneven sidewalks are common.

dailyLiving.simple: PedidosYa and Uber Eats cover parts of Guatemala City and larger towns. Ask locally about water and pharmacy access, especially before rural travel.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Check PedidosYa/Uber Eats at your exact address; service is concentrated in cities and larger towns. Confirm local phone and payment requirements.

Health and water: Use sealed or treated water unless your accommodation confirms local guidance. Pharmacies are common in towns, but rural stock varies; bring essential prescriptions in original packaging.

Food and payment: GTQ cash is useful for markets and smaller businesses. Ask about ingredients, spice, and dietary needs; check service charges on restaurant bills.

socialCode.simple: Guatemala is multilingual; ask which language is preferred. At churches and Maya sites, follow local guidance and ask before photographing people or ceremonies.
socialCode.detailed:
Language: Spanish and many Maya languages are spoken. Ask respectfully before switching language or photographing traditional dress.

Visits: Ask about shoes and gifts in homes; follow the host's cues. Dress modestly at religious sites and observe site-specific community rules.

Photography: Ask permission before photographing people, markets, ceremonies, or private property. Follow restrictions at archaeological and sacred sites.

preArrival.simple: Before planning travel, review current official advisories and entry requirements; route and service availability can change rapidly. Verify any flight with the carrier and airport authority.
preArrival.detailed:
Security and routes: Conditions can change quickly and affect flights, roads, hotels, and public services. Review your government's latest travel advice and consult official Haitian authorities before deciding whether to travel.

Entry: Visa and document rules depend on nationality and purpose. Check Haiti's Ministry of Foreign Affairs or nearest embassy and the airline's boarding requirements.

Preparation: Confirm accommodation, ground transport, communications, medical access, and contingency plans directly with trusted local contacts. Do not rely on generic schedules or app coverage.

arrival24h.simple: Haiti uses 110 V / 60 Hz Type A/B sockets, with local variation and power interruptions. Confirm electricity, communications, payment, and transfer arrangements in advance.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 110 V / 60 Hz, Type A and B sockets are reported; outages and voltage variation can occur. Check lodging backup power and device requirements.

Connectivity and money: Carrier coverage and card/ATM access are variable. Confirm working arrangements with your local contact and carry only the amount of cash needed for the planned route.

Arrival: Airport operations and transport availability may change. Pre-arrange a trusted pickup through your accommodation/local contact and verify current official notices before departure.

mobility.simple: Do not assume normal public transit or ride-hailing is operating. Check current advisories and locally verified transport for each trip; avoid publishing sensitive routes.
mobility.detailed:
Service status: Public transport, roads, and commercial services can be disrupted. Verify each journey with trusted local contacts and current official notices.

Transport arrangements: If travel proceeds, use a known, pre-arranged driver and confirm route/time shortly before departure. Do not rely on an unverified app listing.

Walking and safety: Follow local security guidance and avoid routes or times advised against by authorities. Keep plans flexible and maintain communications with your host/contact.

sources.topic: Haiti Ministry of Public Works, Transport and Communications

dailyLiving.simple: Assume delivery, pharmacy, water, and payment availability are location- and security-dependent. Confirm essentials through accommodation or trusted local contacts before travel.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Food and delivery: Do not rely on delivery apps or normal business hours without current local confirmation. Arrange meals and supplies through a trusted contact.

Water and health: Use sealed water. Confirm clinic/pharmacy operating status and bring essential medication in original packaging, subject to import rules.

Payments and connectivity: Card networks, ATMs, mobile service, and cash availability can be disrupted. Confirm lawful, safe payment arrangements and carry contingency supplies appropriate to official advice.

socialCode.simple: Follow local hosts' and authorities' direction. Ask before photos; avoid photographing security activity, infrastructure, or people without consent.
socialCode.detailed:
Visits: Use a trusted local intermediary where appropriate. Ask about greetings, shoes, gifts, and language preferences; customs vary by household.

Language: Haitian Creole is widely used; French is also used in formal contexts. Ask which language is preferred.

Photography and privacy: Seek consent before photographing people or property. Respect security, privacy, and community guidance, especially during sensitive events.

preArrival.simple: Compare Tegucigalpa (TGU), San Pedro Sula (SAP), and island gateways with Google Flights/Skyscanner. Check Honduras entry rules and current official travel advisories.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: SAP and TGU serve mainland itineraries; Roatán (RTB) and other island airports serve Bay Islands trips. Compare routes and include onward ground/boat transfers.

Entry: Visa and permitted-stay rules depend on nationality, passport, and CA-4 travel. Check Honduras' immigration authority and your government's current advice before booking.

Climate and packing: Caribbean coast, highlands, and Bay Islands weather differ; storm season can disrupt flights/ferries. Check forecasts and advisories; pack rain and sun protection.

arrival24h.simple: Honduras uses 110 V / 60 Hz Type A/B sockets and lempira (HNL). Confirm SIM/card coverage and use a verified airport transfer.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 110 V / 60 Hz, Type A and B sockets. Check device input and adapter fit.

Connectivity and payments: HNL cash is useful; USD may be accepted in some tourist zones, but confirm exchange/change. Check local SIM registration, roaming, and card access.

Airport transfer: Airports are in different cities and use separate transport services. Check official passenger information and arrange licensed taxi/hotel pickup; confirm fare and destination.

mobility.simple: Mainland cities use buses and taxis; intercity coaches connect major towns. Bay Islands transport is local and ferry-dependent; verify schedules before connecting.
mobility.detailed:
Urban transit: Buses and taxis provide most city transport; routes and payment vary. Ask accommodation for current stops and known operators.

Intercity and islands: Scheduled coaches serve mainland routes; ferries and small aircraft connect Bay Islands. Check operator notices, weather, and last departures before booking onward travel.

App rides and walking: Availability varies by city. Confirm fare and pickup with a verified service; use marked crossings and plan for heat and limited sidewalks.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery options are concentrated in Tegucigalpa, San Pedro Sula, and tourist areas. Use bottled or treated water and plan pharmacy access outside cities.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Check current local apps and restaurant direct delivery by address; coverage outside major urban areas is limited.

Health and water: Use sealed/treated water unless local guidance confirms otherwise. Carry essential medicines in original packaging and verify import requirements; pharmacy stock varies outside cities.

Food and payment: HNL cash is useful in local markets and smaller towns. Ask about ingredients and allergens; verify charges and tip practices on the bill.

socialCode.simple: Use a courteous Spanish greeting, ask before photos, and follow host guidance on shoes and gifts. Customs vary across mainland and island communities.
socialCode.detailed:
Language and greetings: Spanish is the principal language; English is used in parts of the Bay Islands. Ask which language is preferred.

Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Follow the host's lead on greetings and meals.

Photography and sites: Ask permission before photographing people, homes, or ceremonies. Follow posted rules at religious and heritage sites.

preArrival.simple: AZair for Europe budget flights. Schengen visa: 90/180 rule, passport valid 3+ months. Continental climate: -2°C to 27°C. Smart casual, thermal bath culture.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: BUD (Budapest Ferenc Liszt) primary hub. Wizz Air (Hungarian budget carrier). AZair for European budget flights. Direct booking typical. Train network: MÁV.

Visa & Legal Compliance: Schengen Area member - 90 days within any 180-day period. Passport valid 3 months beyond departure. Hungary-Visa portal for applications.

Climate & Weather: Continental. Budapest: -2°C (Jan) to 27°C (July). Cold winters, hot summers. Pack layers, warm clothes for winter. Thermal bath culture year-round.

Apparel Sourcing: Smart casual in cities. Modest dress for religious sites. Size system: European. Thermal bath wear: swimwear (gender-separated historically). Local brands: Nanushka.

arrival24h.simple: Power: 230V, 50Hz, Type C/F sockets. Fast 4G/5G, eSIM available. NFC contactless growing. 100E bus to Budapest center.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 230V, 50Hz. Type C (Europlug) and Type F (Schuko) sockets. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-f/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 80+ Mbps. 4G coverage 95%, 5G in cities. ISPs: Magyar Telekom, Vodafone HU, Yettel. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, Holafly. Local SIM: Magyar Telekom (~€30/week).

Financial Rails: NFC contactless growing. Cash still widely used. No mobile money. Tipping: 10% (round up).

Airport-to-City: Budapest BUD: 100E bus (HUF900, 20min) or public bus (HUF900, 45min). Official taxi: fixed rate (~HUF8000-10000 to center). Bolt ride-hailing.

mobility.simple: Budapest Metro (4 lines), trams, buses. No informal transit. Bolt ride-hailing. Bubi bike share. Excellent walkability, thermal baths.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Budapest: Metro (4 lines), trams (4/6 tram famous), buses. Integrated ticket (BKK). Szeged, Debrecen: trams, buses. MÁV trains between cities. Apps: BKK FUTÁR, Google Maps.

Informal Transit: Limited. Formal systems dominate. No Matatus/Marshrutka-style informal transit.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Bolt dominant (Hungarian-founded). No Uber. No other ride-hailing. Bike-sharing: Bubi (Budapest), MOL Bubi. E-scooters: Lime, Tier.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Excellent walkability along Danube. Thermal baths central to culture. Sidewalks well-maintained. Pedestrian crossings respected. Historic: Buda Castle, Parliament, Chain Bridge.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: Wolt, Foodpanda, NetPincér. Alcohol: supermarket sales, no restrictions. Pharmacy: many OTC, antibiotics Rx. Tap water safe. Paprika culture.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: Wolt (Estonian, but popular in Hungary), Foodpanda, NetPincér (Hungarian). Local: Kifli (grocery). Grocery delivery: Tesco, Spar. Delivery hours limited.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, drogériák (drugstores). No state monopoly. Drinking age 18. Tokaji wine, pálinka (fruit brandy) culture. Tipping expected.

Pharmacy: Many OTC medications. Antibiotics Rx-only. Pharmacies marked with green cross. Gyógyszertár (pharmacy) not in supermarkets. 24h pharmacies in cities.

Beverage & Dietary: Tap water potable nationwide, excellent quality. Zero-sugar options available. Local: Unicum (herbal liqueur), paprika-spiced dishes. Hungarian cuisine: gulyás (goulash), paprikás, töltött káposzta (stuffed cabbage). Paprika integral.

Buffet Protocols: Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional: one-plate with refills. Hungarian breakfast buffets. No restrictions on refills.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: avoid chrysanthemums (death), wine/pálinka OK. Shoes removed in homes. Dog-friendly (restaurants). Thermal bath culture, reserved demeanor.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Flowers: odd numbers preferred. Avoid chrysanthemums (death). Wine, pálinka, local food appropriate. Host gifts expected. Unwrap immediately.

Household Norms: Shoes removed in homes. Follow host's lead. Separate house shoes provided.

Companion Pet Culture: Dog-friendly. Dogs allowed in restaurants (patios), public transport. Stray dogs rare. Cat culture present.

Behavioral Matrix: Individualistic, thermal-bath-culture-focused. Thermal baths central to social life. Punctuality: 5-10 min grace socially. Tipping: 10% (round up). Personal space respected. Reserved initially, warm in bathhouses. Direct communication. Paprika spice culture. History: Austro-Hungarian Empire, communism.

preArrival.simple: Use Google Flights/Skyscanner for international comparisons and AirAsia MOVE/Traveloka for Southeast Asian and domestic combinations. Indonesia's eVisa eligibility depends on passport and entry point.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Jakarta (CGK), Bali/Denpasar (DPS), and Surabaya (SUB) serve different islands. AirAsia MOVE and Traveloka compare regional routes; verify airport, baggage, and inter-island transfer with the operating airline.

Entry: Indonesia's official eVisa/eVOA system lists eligibility, entry ports, and stay conditions. Check evisa.imigrasi.go.id for your passport before booking; requirements may vary by purpose and change.

Climate and packing: Tropical conditions vary by island and rainy season. Check local forecasts and volcano/air-quality notices; pack breathable clothing, rain protection, and modest attire for temples.

arrival24h.simple: Indonesia uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type C/F sockets. QRIS is a national QR payment standard, but visitor access depends on bank/app; carry rupiah cash.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check device input before use.

Connectivity and payment: Buy a SIM/eSIM through an authorized provider and confirm registration. QRIS is widely accepted domestically, but visitors may not be able to activate a compatible wallet; keep Indonesian rupiah (IDR) and card backup.

Airport transfer: Jakarta CGK and Bali DPS have official transport operators and app pickup zones. Check the airport page and terminal-specific pickup rules; confirm fare and destination before leaving.

mobility.simple: Jakarta has MRT, commuter rail, buses, and TransJakarta BRT; GoJek and Grab are common in cities. Inter-island ferries/flights require separate planning.
mobility.detailed:
Jakarta: MRT, KRL commuter rail, TransJakarta buses, and airport rail serve different corridors. Use operator apps for routes, tickets, and service alerts; payment systems are not fully interchangeable.

Ride-hailing: GoJek and Grab provide car and motorcycle trips in many urban areas. Confirm pickup point, vehicle, and fare in-app; services are limited outside major towns.

Inter-island: Flights and ferries connect the archipelago; schedules depend on weather and season. Confirm port/terminal and allow buffers. Walking conditions and traffic vary widely.

dailyLiving.simple: GoFood and GrabFood serve many urban areas; check coverage on islands and outside city centres. Use bottled water and verify pharmacy/medicine rules.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: GoFood and GrabFood are common in urban zones; verify exact address, phone, and payment. Coverage falls outside city centres and on smaller islands.

Health and water: Do not assume tap water is potable. Use sealed or treated water. Bring medicines in original packaging and verify Indonesian import restrictions, especially for controlled prescriptions.

Payments and dining: Cash and QRIS/mobile wallets are common but visitor access varies. Ask about ingredients, spice, and halal/dietary requirements; buffet policies are venue-specific.

socialCode.simple: At temples and mosques, follow dress and footwear rules. Ask before photographing people or ceremonies; customs differ across Indonesia's regions.
socialCode.detailed:
Religious sites: Follow posted clothing and footwear requirements; sarongs may be required at some temples. Ask permission before photographing worshippers or ceremonies.

Home and dining: Ask whether to remove shoes and about food preferences. In some settings the right hand is customary for eating or passing items; follow the host's cue.

Language and conduct: Bahasa Indonesia is widely used, with many local languages. Ask politely before photos and avoid generalizing customs across islands or communities.

preArrival.simple: Use AZair for low-cost European combinations and Google Flights/Skyscanner for broad coverage. Sardinia is a separate island-routing problem: compare Cagliari/Olbia/Alghero flights with ferries.
preArrival.detailed:
National routing: Rome (FCO), Milan (MXP/LIN), and other regional airports serve different itineraries. Compare Google Flights/Skyscanner with AZair and confirm baggage/airport with the operating airline.

Sardinia: Cagliari (CAG), Olbia (OLB), and Alghero (AHO) have different seasonal routes. Compare flights with ferries from mainland ports; use the island tourism/port operator timetable and include the port-to-lodging transfer.

Entry and climate: Italy is in Schengen; eligibility depends on nationality and prior 90/180 days. Weather varies from Alps to Mediterranean islands; check region-specific forecasts and pack layers.

arrival24h.simple: Italy uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type F and L sockets. Sardinia uses the same standard; compare airport/ferry transfer options and check local eSIM/roaming terms.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type F and L sockets. Check device compatibility and whether the accommodation offers grounded Type L outlets.

Connectivity and payments: Euro, cards, and contactless are common; keep cash for small merchants. Check roaming terms and rural coverage, especially in Sardinia's interior.

Arrival: Airport transport differs by city. In Sardinia, Cagliari, Olbia, and Alghero airports serve different areas; check current bus/car-rental/ferry connections with the airport/operator.

mobility.simple: Italy's rail system connects major cities; Sardinia relies more on regional ARST bus/rail and rental cars. Check Trenitalia/Italo and Sardinian operator schedules separately.
mobility.detailed:
Mainland: Trenitalia and Italo serve intercity routes; local transit is municipal. Verify station, train type, reservation, and ticket validation.

Sardinia: ARST runs regional buses and rail services; coverage/frequency is lower in inland areas. Check timetables and return services before day trips; a rental car may be necessary for remote beaches and villages.

Walking: Historic centers have cobbles and restricted-traffic zones (ZTL). Check signs and lodging access before driving; island terrain and summer heat affect walking.

dailyLiving.simple: Deliveroo, Glovo, and local grocery services cover many cities; check exact address. Sardinia island coverage varies by town and season.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Deliveroo and Glovo cover many urban areas; verify address and phone requirements. In Sardinia, service is concentrated in larger towns and may be seasonal.

Health and water: Tap-water guidance is municipal/building-specific; ask locally. Pharmacies are marked farmacia; check duty-pharmacy hours and bring prescriptions in original packaging.

Food and payment: Sardinia has distinct regional food traditions; ask about ingredients and allergens. Euro is used; service charges/coperto and tipping differ by venue, so read the bill.

socialCode.simple: At churches and archaeological sites, follow posted dress and photography rules. In Sardinia, ask about local customs and language preferences rather than assuming mainland norms.
socialCode.detailed:
Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small regional food gift is welcome. Household customs differ by family and region.

Religious and heritage sites: Follow signs on clothing, photography, and access. Ask before photographing people or private property.

Sardinia: Italian is widely used alongside Sardinian and other local varieties. Ask which language is preferred; respect community rules and protected sites.

preArrival.simple: Kingston (KIN) and Montego Bay (MBJ) serve different regions; compare flights and ground transfer together. Check Jamaica's passport-specific entry and immigration guidance.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: KIN serves Kingston/east; MBJ serves the north-west resort corridor. Compare the airport with your final destination and check domestic connections for Portland or other distant areas.

Entry: Jamaica's visa requirements and permitted stay depend on nationality and purpose. Check Passport, Immigration and Citizenship Agency guidance before travel.

Climate and packing: Tropical heat, rainy/hurricane seasons, and mountain conditions vary. Check official weather advisories; pack sun/rain protection and suitable shoes.

arrival24h.simple: Jamaica uses 110 V / 50 Hz Type A/B sockets; JMD is local currency, with USD often used in visitor areas. Confirm airport pickup, SIM, and card/ATM access.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 110 V / 50 Hz, Type A and B sockets. Check device input; frequency differs from some countries.

Connectivity and money: JMD is local currency; USD is accepted by some tourist businesses, but change may be in JMD. Check mobile coverage, SIM registration, ATM fees, and card acceptance.

Airport transfer: KIN and MBJ have separate ground transport. Use authorized taxi dispatch or a pre-arranged hotel transfer and confirm fare/destination.

mobility.simple: Kingston uses JUTC buses; Knutsford Express serves intercity coach routes. Route taxis and private taxis cover gaps; confirm stops, fares, and late return options.
mobility.detailed:
Kingston: JUTC provides scheduled city bus service; check route, fare, and service notices. Coverage and hours vary by corridor.

Intercity: Knutsford Express connects major towns and airports. Confirm terminal, seat, luggage rules, and schedule. Route taxis serve shorter local journeys but use local routes/stops.

Taxis and walking: Use licensed/authorized operators and agree fare in advance. Sidewalks and road lighting vary; follow local safety advice.

dailyLiving.simple: Food delivery varies by city; use restaurant apps/direct ordering only after checking coverage. Ask locally about water, pharmacy hours, and service charges.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: 7Krave and restaurant-direct services are examples to check in Kingston/Montego Bay; verify the address, phone, payment, and current operating zone.

Health and water: Follow local water notices and accommodation advice; use sealed water if uncertain. Check the duty pharmacy and bring prescribed medicines in original packaging.

Food and payment: JMD cash is useful outside large hotels. Ask about ingredients and spice; review the bill for service charge before tipping.

socialCode.simple: Ask before photographing people, especially children or ceremonies. At homes and churches, follow host/site guidance on clothing, shoes, and greetings.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings: English and Jamaican Patois are used; ask which language is comfortable. Begin with a courteous greeting.

Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Follow the host's lead on meals and greetings.

Photography: Ask permission before portraits, private property, or ceremonies. Follow posted rules at churches, heritage sites, and public facilities.

preArrival.simple: Compare direct JAL/ANA fares with Google Flights/Skyscanner; use regional low-cost carriers for domestic hops. Check Japan MOFA visa rules by nationality and stay length.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Tokyo (NRT/HND), Osaka (KIX), and other regional airports serve different itineraries. Compare broad search with JAL, ANA, Peach, and Jetstar Japan; verify airport and baggage for each leg.

Entry: Japan's visa exemption and eVisa availability depend on nationality, trip purpose, and duration. Check MOFA and the relevant embassy before booking; follow current Visit Japan Web/customs instructions if applicable.

Climate and packing: Hokkaido, Tokyo, Kansai, and Okinawa differ substantially; rainy season and typhoon risk are seasonal. Check regional forecasts and pack layers.

arrival24h.simple: Japan uses 100 V / 50 or 60 Hz Type A/B sockets; eastern and western grids differ. Keep some yen and check tourist SIM, airport rail, and IC-card options.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 100 V with Type A/B sockets; frequency is 50 Hz in eastern Japan and 60 Hz in western Japan. Check device compatibility, especially for appliances not rated 100 V.

Connectivity and money: Tourist eSIM/SIM options are available; confirm coverage for rural areas. Cash remains useful alongside cards and transit IC cards; carry yen for small businesses.

Airport transfer: Narita and Haneda are separate airports with different rail/bus connections. Check the airport's current routes, last departures, and ticket options before landing.

mobility.simple: Use NAVITIME/Japan Travel or station signage for rail routes; IC cards such as Suica/PASMO work in many regions but are not universal. Taxi apps include GO.
mobility.detailed:
City and intercity rail: JR, metro, and private rail operators have different fares and coverage. Japan Travel by NAVITIME and official operator sites help plan routes; check last trains and reserved-seat rules.

Payment: Suica/PASMO and other IC cards are accepted widely but not everywhere or on every rural service. Keep a backup ticket/payment method and check fare gates.

Taxis and walking: GO taxi app and local dispatch services operate in many cities. Sidewalks are orderly in many centres but narrow in older districts; follow left-side traffic and station etiquette.

dailyLiving.simple: Uber Eats, Demae-can, and Wolt cover many city addresses; check postcode and phone requirements. Tap water is generally treated; bring medication in original packaging.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery and shops: Uber Eats, Demae-can, and Wolt are available in many urban areas; verify the exact address, phone, and payment method. Convenience stores are widespread, but regional stock varies.

Health and water: Municipal tap water is generally treated; follow local notices. Check Japan's medication import rules in advance, especially for prescription or controlled medicines.

Food and payment: Cash, IC cards, and cards are all useful. Ask about allergens and dietary needs; buffet rules depend on the venue and may be time-limited.

sources.topic: Japan National Tourism Organization visitor guide

socialCode.simple: Remove shoes where indicated, keep voices low on transit, and follow temple signage. Ask before photos; gift customs depend on the relationship and occasion.
socialCode.detailed:
Home and lodging: Remove shoes where the entryway or signage indicates; slippers may be provided. Follow local rules at ryokan, temples, and certain restaurants.

Transit and dining: Keep phone calls quiet on public transport and follow queue markings. Use serving utensils for shared dishes and avoid sticking chopsticks upright in rice.

Photography and gifts: Ask permission before photographing people or private property. Gifts are occasion-specific; choose modest, well-presented items only when invited or appropriate.

sources.topic: Japan National Tourism Organization etiquette guide

preArrival.simple: Compare Nairobi (NBO) and coastal/regional routes with Google Flights/Skyscanner and Kenya Airways or Jambojet directly. Kenya requires an ETA for most visitors; check eligibility.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Nairobi (NBO) is the main international hub; Mombasa (MBA) and regional airports serve coast and safari circuits. Compare broad flight search with Kenya Airways, Jambojet, and operating carriers; check baggage and transfer time.

Entry: Kenya uses an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) system. Requirements and exemptions vary by nationality, trip, and transit; apply and check status only through etakenya.go.ke before travel.

Climate and packing: Elevation makes Nairobi cooler than the coast; safari regions vary by season. Check forecast and park conditions. Pack sun/rain protection, modest city clothing, and neutral outdoor layers where appropriate.

arrival24h.simple: Kenya uses 240 V / 50 Hz Type G sockets. M-Pesa is central to daily payments, but visitor registration and account functionality vary; carry a card and some KES cash.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 240 V / 50 Hz, Type G sockets. Check device voltage and bring a compatible adapter.

Connectivity and payments: Safaricom SIM registration requires accepted ID; verify visitor requirements and roaming before travel. M-Pesa is widely used, but don't assume a visitor can open or fund an account. Carry Kenyan shillings (KES) and a card backup.

Airport transfer: Nairobi JKIA provides current passenger and ground-transport information. Use official taxi/app pickup points; agree destination and confirm fare before leaving.

mobility.simple: Nairobi relies on matatus, buses, and ride-hailing; Mombasa and other cities differ. Use official SGR booking for Nairobi–Mombasa rail and confirm station transfers.
mobility.detailed:
Nairobi: Matatus and buses serve extensive routes but stops and fares are local. Ask a trusted local or use a route app; check destination before boarding.

Rail and intercity: Kenya Railways' Madaraka Express connects Nairobi and Mombasa; book through the official platform and confirm departure station, ID requirements, and last-mile transport.

Ride-hailing and walking: Uber, Bolt, and Little operate in some cities. Verify plate/pickup and use official booking. Walkability varies by district; plan for heat, road crossings, and uneven pavements.

sources.topic: Kenya National Transport and Safety Authority

dailyLiving.simple: Glovo and Uber Eats cover some Nairobi addresses; check zone availability. Use bottled or treated water unless local authorities/accommodation confirm otherwise.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Glovo and Uber Eats are available in selected urban zones; enter the exact address and check phone/payment options. Coverage outside Nairobi and Mombasa is limited.

Water and health: Water safety varies by source and building; use sealed or treated water if uncertain. Pharmacies are common in cities, but bring essential medication in original packaging and confirm import rules.

Payments and food: M-Pesa is common but visitor access is not guaranteed. KES cash/cards remain useful. Try local dishes and ask about allergens; check venue service charges and tipping expectations.

socialCode.simple: Kenya is multilingual and culturally diverse. Ask before photos, especially of people or government/security sites; follow host cues on greetings and home footwear.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings and language: English and Swahili are widely used alongside many local languages. Ask which language is preferred and use a courteous greeting; customs vary by community.

Home visits and dining: Ask about shoes and whether a small gift is welcome. Follow the host's serving customs and ask about dietary needs.

Photography and safety: Ask before photographing people, markets, or private property. Respect restrictions at government, border, military, and wildlife sites.

preArrival.simple: For Laos, compare flights via Bangkok or Hanoi with Google Flights/Skyscanner; AirAsia MOVE and Traveloka can help stitch regional legs. Check Laos e-Visa eligibility by nationality.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Vientiane (VTE) is the main gateway; Luang Prabang (LPQ) and Pakse (PKZ) serve regional itineraries. Compare broad search with AirAsia MOVE/Traveloka for Southeast Asian connections, then verify routes with Lao Airlines and the operating carrier.

Entry: Laos e-Visa eligibility, ports of entry, and stay conditions are passport-specific. Check the official eVisa portal before booking and use only listed border checkpoints.

Climate and packing: Tropical monsoon climate, with hot/rainy and cooler/drier periods; northern highlands can be cooler. Check forecasts, bring rain protection and modest temple clothing.

arrival24h.simple: Laos uses 230 V / 50 Hz and Type A, B, C, E, and F sockets; check the specific lodging outlet. Keep kip cash for small payments and network outages.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz; Type A, B, C, E, and F outlets are reported. Check the plug at your lodging and device label; an adapter does not convert voltage.

Connectivity and money: Check roaming/SIM availability and registration. The Lao kip (LAK) is local currency; cash is useful, especially outside Vientiane. Card and wallet acceptance is venue-dependent.

Airport transfer: VTE and LPQ have local transfer options that change. Confirm the airport's current passenger information, use marked taxi counters or hotel-arranged transport, and agree the fare before departure.

mobility.simple: Vientiane mainly uses buses and taxis; Loca ride-hailing coverage is city-specific. Laos-China Railway is useful for major north-south stops; book through official channels.
mobility.detailed:
Vientiane: City buses serve selected corridors; check current timetables and payment locally. Loca is a local ride app, but coverage depends on location and network access.

Intercity: Laos-China Railway connects Vientiane with northern destinations; confirm current timetable, station, ticket name, and boarding rules through the official railway/booking channel. Coaches serve other routes.

Walking: Heat, limited sidewalks, and traffic can make walking difficult outside central districts. Plan short routes, use marked crossings, and avoid assuming rural transport runs frequently.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery-app coverage is limited and address-dependent outside Vientiane. Use sealed or treated water and carry essential medicines for rural travel.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Daily services: Delivery and grocery apps have limited coverage; ask your accommodation which service currently reaches the address. Cash may be needed for small shops and transport.

Health and water: Do not assume tap water is potable. Use sealed bottled or properly treated water. Pharmacies are less comprehensive outside larger towns; carry essential medication in original packaging and check import rules.

Food and dining: Lao food often uses herbs, sticky rice, and shared dishes; ask about fish sauce, allergens, and spice. Service and buffet rules vary by venue; check before ordering.

socialCode.simple: At temples, cover shoulders and knees and remove shoes where instructed. Ask before photographing people or ceremonies; follow a host's cues at home.
socialCode.detailed:
Temples and homes: Dress modestly at religious sites and remove shoes where asked. In homes, ask your host about footwear and gifts.

Monastic settings: Do not touch monks without invitation; follow posted visitor rules and ask before photographing ceremonies or people.

Dining and language: Lao is the primary language; English availability varies. Be courteous, ask about ingredients, and follow the host's lead on shared food.

preArrival.simple: AZair for Europe budget flights. Schengen visa: 90/180 rule, passport valid 3+ months. Baltic climate: -5°C to 22°C. Smart casual, Art Nouveau.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: RIX (Riga) primary hub. airBaltic (flag carrier). AZair for European budget flights. Direct booking typical. Train network: Pasažieru vilciens.

Visa & Legal Compliance: Schengen Area member - 90 days within any 180-day period. Passport valid 3 months beyond departure. Latvia-Visa portal for applications.

preArrival.simple: Direct booking on Mexican carriers. Visa-free for many (FMM form). Varied climate: CDMX 12°C to 26°C, Cancún 22°C to 33°C. Casual dress, modest for churches.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight Consolidators & Hub Routing: MEX (Mexico City), CUN (Cancún), GDL (Guadalajara) major hubs. Aeroméxico (flag carrier), Volaris, VivaAerobus budget carriers. Direct booking typical. No regional consolidator standard.

Visa & Legal Compliance: Visa-free for 65+ countries (US, Canada, EU, UK, Japan). FMM (Forma Migratoria Múltiple) required for all (free at airport, valid 180 days). Visa required for others. Passport valid 6 months beyond stay.

Climate & Weather: Varied by altitude/region. Mexico City: 12°C (Jan) to 26°C (July). Cancún: 22°C to 33°C. Guadalajara: 11°C to 28°C. Check specific destination. Altitude affects temperature (CDMX 2,240m). Rainy season May-Oct.

Apparel Sourcing: Casual acceptable. Modest dress for churches (no shorts, cover shoulders). Beach culture in coastal areas. Size system: US sizing. Sun protection essential.

arrival24h.simple: Power: 127V, 60Hz, Type A/B sockets. 4G/5G good, eSIM available. NFC contactless growing. Authorized taxi booths at airports.
arrival24h.detailed:
Electrical Infrastructure: 127V, 60Hz (some areas 220V). Type A (two flat pins) and Type B (two flat + ground pin) sockets. Visual reference: https://www.power-plugs-sockets.com/type-a/

Connectivity & ISP: Average broadband 50+ Mbps. 4G coverage 92%, 5G in cities. ISPs: Telcel, Movistar, AT&T Mexico. Tourist eSIM: Airalo, Holafly. Local SIM: Telcel (~$40/week).

Financial Rails: NFC contactless growing (SPEI system). Cash still widely used. No mobile money. Tipping: 10-15% expected in restaurants, round up for services.

Airport-to-City: Mexico City MEX: Authorized taxi only (airport booth, ~$25-35 to center). Metro Line 5 (₺5, 30min). Cancún: ADO bus ($12, 30min) or authorized taxi (~$35-50). Never use unauthorized taxis at airports.

mobility.simple: CDMX Metro (12 lines), Metrobus (BRT). Pesero (informal minibuses). Uber, Didi ride-hailing. Ecobici bike share. Walkability: good in centers, security concerns.
mobility.detailed:
Urban Transit Grids: Mexico City: 12 Metro lines, Metrobus BRT, trolleybus. Integrated card: Metrobús card. Guadalajara: SITE, Macrobus. Monterrey: Metrorrey. Apps: CDMX Mobility, Moovit.

Informal Transit: Pesero (informal minibuses) operating fixed routes, frequent but unregulated. Colectivos (shared taxis) common. Informal transit significant in cities.

Micro-Mobility & Ride-Hailing: Uber, Didi dominant. No Bolt. Bike-sharing: Ecobici (CDMX), MiBici (GDL). E-scooters: Grin, Spin in CDMX.

Pedestrian Infrastructure: Variable. Excellent in Polanco, Roma, Condesa. Crowded in historic center. Security concerns in some areas at night. Sidewalk quality varies. Pedestrian crossings: use zebra crossings, cars may not yield.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery: Rappi, Didi Food, Uber Eats. Alcohol: supermarket sales, no restrictions. Pharmacy: many OTC, antibiotics Rx. Tap water: not safe - boil or bottle.
dailyLiving.detailed:
E-Commerce & Delivery: Dominant: Rappi (Colombian, extensive), Didi Food, Uber Eats. Local: Cornershop (grocery). Grocery delivery: Walmart, Chedraui. 24/7 Rappi delivery culture.

Retail & Alcohol: Open sales in supermarkets, convenience stores (OXXO). No state monopoly. Drinking age 18. Tequila/mezcal culture. Tipping expected.

Pharmacy: Many OTC medications. Antibiotics Rx-only (enforced). Pharmacies: Farmacias del Ahorro, Benavides. Farmacias Similares (generic). 24h pharmacies common.

Beverage & Dietary: **Tap water not safe** - boil or use bottled water. Zero-sugar options available. Local: Coca-Cola (very popular), aguas frescas. Corn tortillas, beans, chiles staple.

Buffet Protocols: Hotel buffets: multi-plate common. Traditional: one-plate with refills. Comida corrida (set menu) common. Sharing dishes typical. No restrictions on refills.

socialCode.simple: Gifts: avoid yellow marigolds (death), wine/food OK. Shoes removed in some homes. Dog-friendly in cities. Hospitality, family focus, personal space moderate.
socialCode.detailed:
Gift-Giving Etiquette: Flowers: avoid yellow marigolds (associated with death). Odd numbers preferred. Wine, tequila, regional food appropriate. Host gifts expected for dinner.

Household Norms: Shoes often removed in homes. Follow host's lead.

Companion Pet Culture: Dog-friendly in cities, less in rural areas. Dogs in restaurants (patios). Stray dogs common in rural areas. Cat culture present.

Behavioral Matrix: Collectivist, family-focused. Warm, expressive culture. Physical greetings: handshake (formal), hug/kiss on cheek (friends). Punctuality: 30-60 min grace socially (mañana culture). Tipping: 10-15% expected. Personal space moderate. Siesta tradition fading but late lunches (2-4pm) common.

preArrival.simple: Compare Chișinău flights with Google Flights or Skyscanner; AZair can help find low-cost European legs. Verify Moldova's entry rules for your passport before booking.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight search and routing: Chișinău International Airport (RMO, formerly KIV) is the main air gateway. Google Flights and Skyscanner are useful for broad comparisons; AZair specializes in low-cost European combinations. Confirm each itinerary with the airline. Iași can be a nearby alternative for some trips, but compare the full ground transfer and border crossing, not just the airfare.

Entry rules: Visa requirements depend on nationality, purpose, and length of stay. Check current guidance from Moldova's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant embassy before travel.

Climate and packing: Moldova has cold winters and warm to hot summers. Check forecasts for Chișinău and any rural or vineyard stops; pack layers, rain protection, and suitable walking shoes.

arrival24h.simple: Chișinău uses 220 V / 50 Hz Type C and F sockets. Carry some Moldovan lei and verify roaming, SIM, and card options for your provider.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check device labels before plugging in; a travel adapter does not convert voltage.

Connectivity and money: Check your carrier's Moldova roaming and eSIM coverage before departure. The local currency is the Moldovan leu (MDL); card acceptance and ATM availability are better planned around your exact destination than assumed nationwide. Keep a modest cash backup.

Airport transfer: Check the airport's current transport page for bus, taxi, and service updates. Use the marked taxi area or a verified booking, and confirm the drop-off point and fare before starting the trip.

mobility.simple: Chișinău has trolleybuses, buses, and shared minibuses. Check route and ticket details locally; intercity departures are operator- and station-specific.
mobility.detailed:
Chișinău: Trolleybuses and buses form the main urban network; shared minibuses (rutieras) also run on city and regional corridors. Confirm route, stop, payment, and schedule locally because services can change.

Intercity: Scheduled coaches and rail serve different routes and stations. Check the operator's current timetable and departure location, especially for a cross-border trip.

Ride-hailing and walking: Verify app coverage at your address before relying on it. Sidewalk quality and crossing conditions vary; inspect the route and allow extra time outside the central area.

dailyLiving.simple: Glovo coverage is address-dependent in Chișinău; check the app before relying on delivery. Ask locally about tap water and pharmacy access.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery and shopping: Check Glovo or other current local listings with your exact address; coverage and phone-number requirements differ outside the capital. Confirm grocery delivery and store hours with the provider.

Pharmacy and water: Bring prescription medicines in original packaging and confirm import rules. Water quality can vary by source and building; ask your host or use sealed/treated water if uncertain. Find the nearest open pharmacy after arrival.

Food and service: Moldovan wine, placinte, and regional dishes are widely associated with local food culture. Ask about ingredients and dietary needs. Check the bill for service charges; tipping is discretionary and venue-dependent.

socialCode.simple: For a home visit, ask about shoes and gifts; a small local food item is a considerate option. Ask which language your host prefers and follow their lead.
socialCode.detailed:
Hosting and greetings: Moldovan households and language preferences vary. Begin politely, ask whether Romanian or another language is preferred, and follow the host's lead on greetings and footwear.

Gifts and dining: A small food or wine gift may suit a host who drinks, but check preferences and avoid assuming alcohol is appropriate. Ask about dietary restrictions and observe the household's meal customs.

Public conduct: Ask permission before photographing people or private property. Etiquette differs by person and context; use local cues rather than relying on national stereotypes.

preArrival.simple: Compare Podgorica and Tivat flights using Google Flights/Skyscanner and AZair for low-cost European legs. Visa rules depend on nationality; check the government source before booking.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Podgorica (TGD) and Tivat (TIV) serve different parts of the country. Routes are seasonal; compare Google Flights/Skyscanner and AZair, then confirm schedule and baggage with the airline.

Entry: Montenegro is outside Schengen. Visa eligibility, permitted stay, and passport validity depend on nationality and trip details; use the current Montenegrin government or embassy guidance.

Climate and clothing: The coast has Mediterranean conditions; inland and mountain areas can be much colder and wetter. Check the forecast for each stop and pack layers, rain protection, and suitable footwear for steep old towns.

arrival24h.simple: Montenegro uses the euro and 230 V / 50 Hz Type C/F sockets. TGD and TIV have separate transfer options; check the official airport pages for current details.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check device voltage before plugging in.

Connectivity and money: Euro is used, although Montenegro is not an EU or euro-area member. Card and ATM access varies by town; keep some cash and check roaming with your carrier.

Airport transfer: Podgorica and Tivat airports serve different destinations. Check Airports of Montenegro's current flight and passenger information; verify bus departures locally and use marked taxi services with the fare agreed before travel.

mobility.simple: Podgorica and coastal towns rely on buses and taxis; Montenegro Rail serves the Bar–Podgorica–Bijelo Polje corridor. Check live operator schedules.
mobility.detailed:
Rail: ŽPCG publishes a timetable and online ticket links for domestic and international services. The Bar–Podgorica–Bijelo Polje line is the main passenger rail corridor; verify current service and station details.

Buses: Intercity coaches connect Podgorica, the coast, and inland towns. Confirm terminal, operator, luggage rules, and departure time; schedules can be seasonal.

Local trips: Ride-hailing availability is limited and city-specific. Agree taxi fares before departure. Kotor and other old towns have steep, uneven pedestrian routes.

dailyLiving.simple: Glovo coverage is address-specific in larger towns. Ask locally about water and pharmacy hours, especially on the coast outside peak season.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery and shops: Check Glovo or local listings for the exact address; availability is strongest in larger towns and varies seasonally. Confirm opening hours, especially outside summer.

Health and water: Ask your accommodation about local water supply and the nearest open pharmacy. Bring essential medication in original packaging and verify import requirements.

Food and payment: Coastal menus often feature seafood; inland dishes differ. Ask about ingredients and allergens. Euro is used; check bills for any service charge and tip at your discretion.

socialCode.simple: Ask before photographing people or religious sites. At home, follow your host's lead on shoes and gifts; customs differ between households and regions.
socialCode.detailed:
Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small local food gift is welcome. Do not assume alcohol is appropriate for every host.

Religious and heritage sites: Follow posted clothing and photography rules; ask permission before photographing people or private property.

Conversation: Use a polite greeting and ask which language is preferred. Avoid generalizations about regional identity or customs.
