preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Maputo (MPM) is the primary international gateway; Beira (BEW), Nampula (APL), and Vilankulo (VNX) serve regional trips. Compare broad search with LAM and other operating carriers; confirm baggage and connections.

Entry: Mozambique's eVisa/ETA process and eligibility depend on passport nationality and entry point. Check the official eVisa portal and current Ministry of Interior guidance; do not rely on third-party visa agents.

Climate and packing: Coastal heat, rainy-season storms, and southern/inland conditions differ. Check cyclone and flood advisories for the season. Pack sun protection, rain gear, and breathable clothing.

arrival24h.simple: Mozambique uses 220 V / 50 Hz Type C, F, and M outlets. Keep meticais (MZN) and confirm ATM/card access, SIM registration, and airport transport locally.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 50 Hz; Type C, F, and M sockets are reported. Check the outlet and device label before use; an adapter does not convert voltage.

Connectivity and payments: Check local SIM registration and roaming. Metical (MZN) cash is important; card acceptance and ATM coverage are concentrated in cities and larger hotels.

Airport transfer: Maputo Airport transport and taxi arrangements can change. Arrange hotel pickup or use a clearly identified taxi; agree destination and fare before leaving.

mobility.simple: Maputo uses buses and shared chapas; intercity coaches and flights suit longer distances. Check the route and fare locally; do not assume ride-hailing nationwide.
mobility.detailed:
Maputo: Buses and shared chapas serve urban corridors. Routes and stops can be informal; ask a trusted local, confirm destination/fare before boarding, and keep small MZN notes.

Intercity: Coaches and domestic flights connect major cities, but journey times and service frequency vary. Confirm operator, station, luggage, and schedule before travel.

Taxis and walking: App-based transport is not uniform across the country. Use a licensed/known provider and agree the fare. Sidewalk and road conditions vary; avoid assuming a route is pedestrian-friendly.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery options are limited outside central Maputo. Use sealed or treated water and plan pharmacy/medication needs before beach or park trips.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery and shopping: App delivery is concentrated in urban areas. Confirm address coverage and payment directly with the service; smaller towns and islands may have no app-based option.

Health and water: Use sealed bottled or appropriately treated water. Carry essential medicines in original packaging and verify import rules; pharmacy stock and opening hours vary by city.

Food and payment: Seafood is common on the coast; ask about ingredients and allergens. MZN cash is useful for local markets. Check service charge and buffet terms at each venue.

socialCode.simple: Portuguese is the official language, with many local languages. Ask before photos and follow your host's cues on shoes, greetings, and home-visit gifts.
socialCode.detailed:
Language and greetings: Portuguese is used in official settings; local languages are common in daily life. Ask which language is preferred and greet politely.

Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is appropriate. Customs vary by household and region.

Photography and public sites: Ask permission before photographing people, homes, or ceremonies. Follow posted rules at religious and government sites.

preArrival.simple: Windhoek (WDH) is the main gateway; compare Google Flights/Skyscanner with Airlink and regional carriers. Namibia's visa policy changed recently, so check eligibility by passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Hosea Kutako (WDH) serves Windhoek; Walvis Bay (WVB) and regional airports support coastal and safari routes. Compare broad search, then check Airlink/operating carriers and ground-transfer distances.

Entry: Namibia introduced new visa requirements for some nationalities in 2025. Check the Ministry of Home Affairs official visa portal for your passport, entry point, length, and current fees before booking.

Climate and packing: Desert conditions mean hot days, cold nights, and long dry drives. Check seasonal road and weather conditions; pack layers, sun protection, and enough water for remote routes.

arrival24h.simple: Namibia uses 220 V / 50 Hz Type D and M sockets. Carry Namibia dollars or South African rand; ATM/card access declines on remote safari routes.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 50 Hz, Type D and M sockets. Check accommodation outlet and device labels; carry a compatible adapter.

Connectivity and money: Local SIM registration and rural coverage vary. Namibia dollar (NAD) is pegged to and commonly used alongside South African rand (ZAR); keep cash for fuel and remote stops.

Arrival transfer: WDH is outside central Windhoek. Confirm shuttle, rental-car, or hotel pickup in advance; use licensed providers and verify the pickup point.

mobility.simple: Namibia is a long-distance, car-oriented destination; buses connect some towns, while safari routes often require a rental 4x4 or organized transfer.
mobility.detailed:
Intercity: Scheduled coaches serve selected corridors, but frequency is limited. Confirm departure point, baggage, and return options before booking.

Self-drive: A rental car is common for parks and remote regions; check road surface, fuel range, spare tires, and cross-border rental permission. Avoid driving long distances after dark where possible.

City trips: Windhoek taxis and ride services are limited compared with larger cities. Ask accommodation to arrange a known provider and confirm the fare.

dailyLiving.simple: Delivery is limited outside Windhoek and larger towns. Ask lodges about water and pharmacy access before remote travel; stock food/fuel ahead of long drives.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Shopping and delivery: App delivery is limited; check local listings in Windhoek and buy supplies before entering remote areas. Shop hours can be shorter on weekends and holidays.

Health and water: Ask lodges about the local water source and treatment. Carry essential medicines and a basic travel kit; pharmacies are sparse outside urban centres.

Food and payment: Card access is common in towns, but carry NAD/ZAR cash for remote fuel stations and small operators. Confirm meal ingredients and lodge/service charges in advance.

socialCode.simple: Ask before photographing people or private land. For community visits, follow the guide/host on greetings, gifts, and permissions; respect park and conservation rules.
socialCode.detailed:
Community visits: Use a locally arranged guide where appropriate, ask permission before photographs, and follow guidance on gifts or donations.

Home and lodge customs: Ask about footwear and meal practices; customs vary across communities and accommodation types.

Outdoor conduct: Follow park rules, stay on marked routes where required, and do not approach wildlife. Respect private and communal land boundaries.

preArrival.simple: Managua (MGA) is the main air gateway; compare flights via San Salvador, Panama City, or regional hubs. Check Nicaragua's entry rules and current travel advice by passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: MGA is the main international airport. Compare Google Flights/Skyscanner, then check regional connections and the full ground transfer; service frequencies may change.

Entry: Visa, passport validity, and regional CA-4 stay rules depend on nationality and itinerary. Check Nicaragua's immigration authority or nearest embassy before booking.

Climate and packing: Pacific lowlands are hot; Caribbean regions and highlands have different rain patterns. Check forecasts and advisories; pack sun/rain protection and light layers.

arrival24h.simple: Nicaragua uses 120 V / 60 Hz Type A/B sockets and córdobas (NIO). Confirm roaming and card acceptance; arrange a trusted MGA transfer before arrival.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 120 V / 60 Hz, Type A and B sockets. Check device voltage before use.

Connectivity and payments: NIO is local currency; some visitor businesses accept USD, but change and card acceptance vary. Check SIM/roaming and bank fees.

Airport transfer: Use an arranged shuttle, hotel transfer, or verified taxi. Confirm destination and fare before leaving MGA; road travel times vary by traffic and conditions.

mobility.simple: Managua uses city buses and taxis; intercity coaches and ferries serve major routes. Ask locally about current terminals and schedules rather than assuming app coverage.
mobility.detailed:
Managua: City buses and taxis operate on routes that may be unfamiliar to visitors. Confirm stop, direction, fare, and current service with a trusted local source.

Intercity and islands: Coaches connect major towns; ferries serve Ometepe and other lake/island routes. Verify operator, port, and weather-related notices.

Walking: Sidewalks and lighting vary. Plan short routes in daylight where appropriate, use marked crossings, and check local travel advice for routes and timing.

dailyLiving.simple: App delivery is limited outside Managua and larger towns. Use bottled or treated water unless local guidance confirms safety; bring essential medication for remote trips.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Daily services: Restaurant delivery and online grocery options are concentrated in Managua. Call the business or ask accommodation about current phone/address requirements.

Health and water: Use sealed/treated water if uncertain. Pharmacies are available in towns but stock varies; carry prescribed medication in original packaging and verify import rules.

Food and money: Keep NIO cash for local purchases. Ask about ingredients and dietary needs; check any service charge before tipping.

socialCode.simple: Use a polite Spanish greeting, ask before photographing people, and follow host guidance on shoes and meals. Ask about local expectations rather than assuming.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings: Spanish is the main language; a courteous verbal greeting is a safe default.

Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Customs vary by household.

Photography: Ask permission before photographing people, private homes, or ceremonies. Follow posted rules at religious and heritage sites.

preArrival.simple: Use AZair for low-cost European combinations, plus Google Flights/Skyscanner for broad comparisons. Verify North Macedonia's national entry rules and current airport routes.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Skopje (SKP) is the main hub; Ohrid (OHD) has a smaller, seasonal network. Compare broad searches with Google Flights/Skyscanner and AZair, then confirm route, baggage, and schedule with the airline.

Entry rules: North Macedonia is outside Schengen. Visa eligibility and stay limits depend on passport nationality; verify with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the relevant embassy before travel.

Climate and clothing: Skopje has cold winters and hot summers; Ohrid and mountain areas differ. Check forecasts and pack layers, sun protection, and walking shoes.

arrival24h.simple: North Macedonia uses denar (MKD) and 230 V / 50 Hz Type C/F sockets. Skopje Airport posts current transport choices; carry some cash for small purchases.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check device labels before use.

Connectivity and payment: Check carrier roaming/eSIM availability. Cards are common in Skopje but cash remains useful in smaller towns; local currency is the denar (MKD). Confirm ATM fees with your bank.

Airport transfer: Skopje Airport's passenger guide lists current transport alternatives. Recheck schedules and stops after landing; use a licensed taxi or verified booking and confirm the fare before departure.

sources.topic: Skopje Airport transport and passenger guide

mobility.simple: Skopje primarily uses buses; JSP publishes city transport information. Intercity buses are more useful than rail for many routes; check schedules by corridor.
mobility.detailed:
Skopje: JSP operates city buses. Check current timetables, ticket options, and service notices with the operator; route and payment details can change.

Intercity: Coaches connect Skopje, Ohrid, Bitola, and neighboring capitals. Verify departure terminal and schedule with the carrier; do not assume a rail alternative serves each route.

Taxis and walking: Confirm ride-app coverage at the destination and check the fare before riding. Sidewalks and crossings vary by district; use marked crossings and inspect hilly routes.

dailyLiving.simple: Check Korpa, Wolt, or local listings against your exact Skopje address; coverage outside major cities is limited. Ask locally about water and pharmacy access.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Korpa and Wolt are examples to check in Skopje; app coverage, phone requirements, and payment options vary by neighborhood and city. Confirm service before relying on it.

Health and water: Ask your accommodation about local water guidance and the nearest open pharmacy. Bring prescribed medicines in original packaging and verify import rules.

Food and money: Local dishes include tavče gravče and ajvar; ask about allergens and dietary needs. The denar is the currency. Check receipts for any service charge; tipping is venue-dependent.

socialCode.simple: At churches and mosques, follow posted dress and photography guidance. At home, ask whether to remove shoes and what gift is welcome.
socialCode.detailed:
Home visits: Ask about footwear and gift preferences; a small food item may be appropriate, but follow the host's lead.

Religious sites: Dress respectfully where requested and follow photography rules. Ask permission before photographing people or ceremonies.

Language and etiquette: Macedonian and Albanian are widely used in different communities. Ask which language is preferred, greet politely, and avoid assuming one custom applies everywhere.

preArrival.simple: Compare fares on Google Flights/Skyscanner and Pakistan's Sastaticket.pk, then confirm baggage and ticket terms with the airline. Check the official NADRA visa portal for your passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight search and routing: Islamabad (ISB), Karachi (KHI), and Lahore (LHE) are major gateways. Google Flights and Skyscanner help compare international options; Sastaticket.pk is a Pakistan-focused booking platform. Compare the final fare, baggage, change rules, and payment method, then verify with the operating airline.

Entry: Pakistan's official Online Visa System is managed through NADRA. Eligibility and documents depend on nationality and visa category; apply only through the official portal and wait for the required approval before travel.

Climate and packing: Conditions range from high mountains to hot plains and coast. Check the forecast for each region and season. Pack modest, breathable clothing for cities and sun protection; add warm layers for northern or winter trips.

arrival24h.simple: Pakistan uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type C and D sockets. Confirm visitor SIM rules and card acceptance; keep PKR cash for small purchases or outages.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type C and D sockets. The local diagram appears above; check your device label and bring a suitable adapter.

Connectivity and money: Check visitor SIM registration and eSIM eligibility with the carrier before travel; coverage differs by region. Easypaisa and JazzCash are important domestic payment services, but do not assume a visitor can activate them or that international cards will work everywhere. Keep Pakistani rupees (PKR) available and confirm your bank's international-use settings.

Airport transfer: Islamabad Airport provides current flight and passenger information. Use clearly marked airport transport or a verified ride booking; confirm the vehicle, destination, and fare before departure.

mobility.simple: Islamabad, Lahore, and Karachi have different metro/BRT systems. Use current city operator information; ride-hailing and shared options vary by city.
mobility.detailed:
Urban transit: Islamabad has Metrobus service; Lahore has Metrobus and Orange Line Metro Train; Karachi has the Green Line BRT. Check each operator's latest route, fare, and ticket guidance rather than expecting one national pass.

Shared and app-based trips: Intercity buses, vans, and city-specific ride-hailing options fill gaps in the formal networks. Check current app availability and vehicle details in the city where you are staying; confirm the fare and pickup point.

Walking: Heat, traffic, and sidewalk continuity vary sharply by district. Plan short walks in daylight where appropriate, use marked crossings, and choose a car or transit for exposed or high-speed roads.

dailyLiving.simple: Foodpanda operates in major Pakistani cities, but check address coverage. Use sealed or treated water unless a trusted local source confirms otherwise.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Foodpanda and grocery services are available in many urban areas; confirm the exact address, phone requirements, cash/card options, and delivery hours in the app. Availability is thinner outside major cities.

Food, pharmacies, and water: Halal food is widely available, but ask about ingredients and dietary needs. Do not assume tap water is potable; use sealed bottled or properly treated water. Carry essential medication in original packaging with a prescription and check import rules.

Payments and dining: Cash, cards, and domestic wallets are used differently by merchant and city. Confirm service charges before tipping. Buffet rules are venue-specific; follow posted plate or weight-based pricing rather than assuming unlimited refills.

socialCode.simple: Dress modestly in public and at religious sites; ask before photographing people. At a home visit, follow your host on shoes, greetings, and shared-dish etiquette.
socialCode.detailed:
Dress and greetings: Expectations vary by region and setting. Modest clothing is a considerate default, especially in religious spaces; follow posted rules. Use a polite greeting and let the other person set the level of formality or physical contact.

Home and meals: Ask whether to remove shoes. When sharing food, observe the host's practice; some settings favor using the right hand. Ask about dietary needs and avoid assuming every household follows the same custom.

Photography and behavior: Ask permission before photographing people, homes, or religious ceremonies, and follow restrictions at security-sensitive locations. Avoid broad assumptions about gender, language, or religious practice.

preArrival.simple: Compare Tocumen (PTY) and regional airports with Google Flights/Skyscanner; Copa Airlines connects many Americas routes. Check Panama's nationality-specific entry rules.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Tocumen (PTY) is a major regional hub; Albrook (PAC) and David (DAV) serve domestic/regional trips. Compare broadly and verify terminal/connection time with Copa or the operating carrier.

Entry: Panama's visa requirements, onward-ticket, and permitted stay depend on nationality and travel details. Check the National Migration Service and consular guidance before booking.

Climate and packing: Tropical heat and rainy season affect road, island, and canal-zone travel. Check forecasts; bring sun/rain protection and lightweight clothing.

arrival24h.simple: Panama uses 120 V / 60 Hz Type A/B sockets; the balboa is at par with the US dollar, and USD notes circulate. Confirm metro/airport routes and local SIM coverage.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 120 V / 60 Hz, Type A and B sockets. Check device input and adapter compatibility.

Connectivity and payments: Panama uses balboa coins and US dollar notes; card acceptance is common in the capital but varies elsewhere. Check roaming/SIM setup and retain small bills.

Airport transfer: PTY is outside central Panama City. Metro Line 2, buses, taxis, and shuttles have different ticketing/pickup rules; check Tocumen's current information and use official pickup points.

mobility.simple: Panama City has metro and Metrobus; use current official route/ticket guidance. Intercity buses, ferries, and domestic flights connect provinces and islands.
mobility.detailed:
Panama City: Metro and Metrobus serve major corridors. Check current route maps, reloadable fare media, and service alerts; not all airport/visitor trips use the same ticket.

Intercity and islands: Coach, ferry, and domestic air routes serve different regions. Verify departure terminal/port and weather advisories; island schedules may be limited.

Ride-hailing and walking: Uber and other apps operate in parts of Panama City. Confirm pickup and fare; heat and sidewalk gaps affect walking outside central districts.

dailyLiving.simple: PedidosYa and Uber Eats cover many Panama City addresses; verify province/island coverage. Tap-water and pharmacy advice can vary outside major urban areas.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: PedidosYa and Uber Eats are urban options; enter the exact address and check hours/payment. Service is thinner in rural provinces and islands.

Water and pharmacy: Ask accommodation about municipal/building-specific water notices. Use sealed or treated water if uncertain; check local pharmacy hours and bring prescriptions in original packaging.

Payments and food: USD/PAB are used at par in many transactions, but cards/cash differ by merchant. Ask about ingredients and service charges; tipping is venue-dependent.

preArrival.simple: Compare Manila (MNL) and island airports with Google Flights/Skyscanner, Cebu Pacific, and Philippine Airlines. Complete any required eTravel registration and verify visa rules by nationality.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Manila (MNL) is the main hub; Cebu (CEB), Clark (CRK), and island airports can reduce ground travel. Compare broad search with Cebu Pacific and Philippine Airlines, then confirm terminals and baggage.

Entry: Visa eligibility depends on passport and stay. Check the Philippine Bureau of Immigration and complete the official eTravel registration if required for your trip; requirements can change.

Climate and packing: Tropical climate with regional wet-season and typhoon variation. Monitor PAGASA advisories for storm season; pack light rain protection, sun protection, and footwear for wet streets.

arrival24h.simple: The Philippines uses 220 V / 60 Hz Type A, B, and C sockets. Keep pesos (PHP) cash, and check visitor SIM/eSIM and airport terminal transfers before arrival.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 60 Hz, Types A, B, and C. Check device voltage labels and adapter fit; some older buildings may differ.

Connectivity and payment: Local SIM registration requires accepted ID; verify visitor requirements with Globe or Smart. GCash/Maya may require local verification; keep PHP cash and a card backup.

Airport transfer: Manila has multiple terminals and airport transfer links; confirm your airline terminal and official airport bus/taxi or app pickup details. Allow extra time for traffic.

mobility.simple: Metro Manila has MRT/LRT, buses, and jeepneys; provincial islands rely on ferries, vans, and tricycles. Grab and Angkas are city/coverage-specific.
mobility.detailed:
Metro Manila: LRT/MRT, buses, and jeepneys serve different corridors. Check current route and payment information; service can be crowded and affected by traffic or advisories.

Islands and intercity: Ferries, domestic flights, buses, vans, and tricycles connect regions. Weather can disrupt service; confirm schedules with the operator and leave connection buffers.

Ride-hailing: Grab and motorcycle apps such as Angkas operate in selected cities. Verify pickup/plate in-app, use helmets, and avoid assuming the same service exists on every island.

dailyLiving.simple: Foodpanda and GrabFood cover many urban areas; confirm the exact island/address. Use sealed water unless accommodation gives specific local guidance.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Foodpanda and GrabFood are available in many cities, but not uniformly across islands. Verify address, local phone, payment, and weather-related delivery interruptions.

Water and pharmacy: Use sealed or treated water unless local authorities/accommodation confirm otherwise. Pharmacy access is good in cities but limited in remote areas; carry essential medicines and prescriptions.

Payments and food: PHP cash remains useful, especially on smaller islands. Ask about ingredients and allergens; check service charges and buffet terms at the venue.

socialCode.simple: English and Filipino are widely used, alongside regional languages. Ask before photos; at churches or homes, follow posted/host guidance on dress and shoes.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings and language: English and Filipino are widely used, with regional languages across the islands. Ask which language is preferred and greet politely.

Home and religious visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small gift is welcome. Follow church dress rules and the host's lead at meals.

Photography: Ask permission before photographing people, homes, or ceremonies. Respect local and site-specific restrictions.

preArrival.simple: For low-cost European routes, compare AZair with Google Flights/Skyscanner. Poland is in Schengen; check your passport eligibility and prior 90/180 days.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Warsaw (WAW/WMI), Kraków (KRK), and Gdańsk (GDN) serve major regions. Use AZair for low-cost combinations and Google Flights/Skyscanner for broader itineraries; check airport transfer and baggage before booking.

Entry rules: Poland is in Schengen. Visa eligibility depends on nationality, purpose, and days already spent in the area. Check current European Commission rules and Polish consular guidance.

Climate and packing: Poland has cold winters and warm summers, with mountain conditions changing quickly. Check forecasts, pack layers/rain protection, and use sturdy shoes for cobbles or hiking.

arrival24h.simple: Poland uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type C and E sockets and Polish złoty (PLN). Warsaw Chopin has rail/bus connections; check current timetable and payment options.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type C and E sockets. Check device input and adapter compatibility.

Connectivity and money: Poland uses PLN, not the euro. Cards/contactless are common; keep some cash and choose local-currency payment at terminals to avoid dynamic conversion fees.

Airport transfer: Warsaw Chopin Airport has rail and bus connections; confirm terminal stop, first/last service, and current ticket options. Use official taxi stands or verified ride apps.

mobility.simple: Warsaw has metro, trams, and buses; city tickets are not national rail tickets. PKP Intercity and regional operators publish separate schedules and booking.
mobility.detailed:
Warsaw: Metro, trams, and buses use local ticket zones and validation rules. Check the ZTM route planner and current service notices.

Intercity: PKP Intercity serves major routes; regional operators cover local rail. Confirm train category, station, reservation, and luggage rules in the official booking channel.

Ride-hailing and walking: Uber/Bolt availability is city-specific. Historic streets can be cobbled and winter sidewalks icy; allow time and use marked crossings.

dailyLiving.simple: Pyszne.pl, Wolt, and grocery platforms cover many city addresses; verify postcode. Pharmacies and alcohol sales follow local rules; check opening hours.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Pyszne.pl and Wolt are common urban food apps; grocery availability varies by postcode. Check address and payment methods in-app.

Health and water: Municipal tap water is generally treated, but follow local/building advisories. Bring prescriptions in original packaging and check import rules; pharmacies may have rotating duty hours.

Food and payment: PLN cash and cards are both useful. Ask about allergens and ingredients. Check receipts for service charges; tipping is discretionary.

socialCode.simple: At churches, follow posted dress and photography rules. For a home visit, ask about shoes and gifts; customs vary by household.
socialCode.detailed:
Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Follow the host's lead rather than assuming a universal custom.

Religious and heritage sites: Follow posted clothing and photography guidance. Ask before photographing people, services, or private property.

Communication: Start politely and use formal address in unfamiliar settings; follow the other person's lead. Avoid broad claims about national character.

Entry rules: Portugal is in Schengen. Visa eligibility depends on nationality and prior Schengen days; check current European Commission rules and Portuguese consular guidance.

Connectivity and payments: Euro, cards, and contactless are common in cities. Check roaming terms and keep some cash for small businesses or service interruptions.

Airport transfer: Lisbon, Porto, Faro, Madeira, and Azores airports have different bus, metro, taxi, and shuttle options. Check ANA's current airport-specific transport information and last departures.

mobility.simple: Lisbon and Porto have metro, tram, bus, and rail; CP handles national trains. Island transit differs, and ferries/flights are needed between island groups.
mobility.detailed:
Lisbon and Porto: Metro, tram, and bus networks use city-specific tickets/cards. Check Metro Lisboa, Metro do Porto, and Carris for routes, fares, and disruptions.

Intercity and islands: CP operates mainland rail; island connections require separate local buses, ferries, or flights. Confirm the full itinerary and weather-dependent service before setting out.

Walking and rides: Lisbon and Porto are hilly with cobbled pavements; use sturdy shoes. Uber/Bolt operate in larger cities, but pickup zones and service vary by town.

dailyLiving.simple: Glovo, Uber Eats, and Bolt Food cover many urban addresses; verify island/postcode coverage. Tap-water and pharmacy advice can vary by locality/building.
dailyLiving.detailed:

Health and water: Municipal tap water is generally treated, but follow local notices and accommodation guidance. Check local pharmacy hours and bring prescriptions in original packaging.

Food and payment: Try regional dishes and ask about allergens. Euro and contactless payment are common; review the receipt for service charges. Buffet rules are venue-specific.

socialCode.simple: Use a polite greeting and follow local cues. At churches, follow posted dress/photo rules; ask before photographing people or entering private property.

Language: Portuguese is spoken nationwide, with regional variation in the islands. A courteous greeting is appreciated; ask if English is comfortable rather than assuming.

arrival24h.simple: Romania uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type C/F sockets and the leu (RON). OTP has rail and bus connections; check current airport and operator notices.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Confirm your device supports the voltage; an adapter alone is not a converter.

Connectivity and payment: Romania uses the leu (RON). Cards and contactless are common in cities, but keep cash for small merchants and rural stops. Check roaming/eSIM plans before departure.

Airport transfer: Bucharest OTP is linked to the city by train and bus. Check Bucharest Airports' live passenger information and the rail/bus operator for current timetable, ticket, and station details. Use an official taxi desk or a verified ride booking.

mobility.simple: Bucharest has metro, bus, tram, and trolleybus networks; STB and Metrorex publish routes and fares. CFR serves intercity rail; check delays and station details.
mobility.detailed:
Bucharest: STB operates surface transport and Metrorex the metro. Check each operator's current route, ticket, and validation information; an urban pass may not cover intercity rail.

Intercity: CFR Călători publishes rail schedules and booking. Train times and infrastructure works can affect journeys; confirm the station and latest service notices.

Ride-hailing and walking: Bolt and Uber operate in some cities; compare the licensed pickup and displayed fare. Historic centres have uneven paving and busy traffic; plan crossings carefully.

dailyLiving.simple: Glovo and Wolt serve many urban areas; confirm the exact address. Ask your accommodation about tap water, particularly in older buildings or outside major cities.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Check Glovo or Wolt at your address; coverage and opening hours vary by city and neighborhood. Confirm phone and payment requirements before depending on delivery.

Health and water: Ask locally about building plumbing and municipal notices; use sealed or treated water if uncertain. Locate a duty pharmacy and bring prescriptions in original packaging.

Food and payment: Try sarmale, mici, or regional soups; ask about ingredients and allergens. The leu is used; tipping and service charges vary, so review the receipt. Buffet rules are venue-specific.

socialCode.simple: At churches, follow posted clothing and photography rules. For home visits, ask about shoes and gifts; household practices vary.
socialCode.detailed:
Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Let the host set the pace for greetings and the meal.

Religious and heritage sites: Follow posted dress, photography, and service rules; ask before photographing people or ceremonies.

Conversation: Romanian is the official language; English familiarity varies by place and person. Ask politely which language is comfortable and avoid broad claims about national character.

preArrival.simple: For routes currently offered, compare Aviasales.ru with airline sites; verify routes, payment, and your government's travel advice. Russia's e-visa is limited to eligible nationalities.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight search and routing: Moscow uses multiple airports, including Sheremetyevo (SVO), Domodedovo (DME), and Vnukovo (VKO). Aviasales.ru can surface domestic and regional options; confirm international itinerary, payment acceptance, and ticket terms directly with the carrier. Routes and restrictions change, so check current official travel advice before booking.

Entry: Russia's unified e-visa is available only to eligible nationalities, approved crossing points, and permitted trip purposes. Check the MFA portal for current validity, stay limits, passport rules, and insurance requirements; otherwise consult the relevant consulate.

Climate and packing: Conditions vary greatly across Russia. Research the exact city and season; Moscow winters are cold, while summer temperatures vary. Pack layers and allow for snow/ice in winter.

arrival24h.simple: Moscow uses 220 V / 50 Hz Type C and F sockets. Confirm current card, SIM, and payment access before travel; foreign-issued cards may not work.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check device voltage and use a compatible adapter.

Connectivity and payments: Foreign-issued payment cards and international services can be affected by sanctions and local restrictions. Check with your bank and carrier before departure; do not rely on a foreign card, roaming, or a particular app. Use only lawful payment and communications options.

Airport transfer: Moscow airports have different rail, bus, and taxi connections. Check the arrival airport's current official transport page, then use a marked taxi desk or a verified booking. Confirm the route and fare before leaving the terminal.

mobility.simple: Moscow's metro is extensive; use current Metro/Mos.ru route and ticket information. Intercity rail and taxi services have separate booking systems.
mobility.detailed:
Moscow: The metro, buses, and surface rail cover major areas. Check Moscow Metro's current service notices and ticket options; language, payment, and app access may differ for visitors.

Across cities: Russian Railways (RZD) operates intercity trains; confirm station, ticket name/passport matching, and current service before travel. For trips within Moscow, Yandex Go is a local ride option where available; verify pickup details and fare in-app.

Walking and safety: Winter surfaces can be icy and distances between stations long. Check weather and service alerts, use marked crossings, and follow local instructions at transport facilities.

dailyLiving.simple: Yandex Eats and other delivery options are city-specific. Check local payment compatibility, pharmacy hours, and current rules for medicines you bring.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery and shopping: Yandex Eats and grocery delivery services operate in some cities; check the exact address, language, phone, and payment requirements before relying on them. Availability outside large cities varies.

Pharmacy and water: Bring essential medication in original packaging and verify import rules. Ask your accommodation about local tap-water guidance; use sealed or treated water if unsure. Locate an open pharmacy near your stay.

Payments and food: Local currency is the ruble (RUB). International card access can be restricted; check lawful payment options before travel. Try regional dishes and ask about ingredients. Buffet terms and service charges are set by each venue.

socialCode.simple: At a home visit, ask about shoes and gifts; begin with a polite, formal greeting. Follow posted rules and ask before photographing people or official sites.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings and hosting: A measured, polite greeting is a safe start. In private homes, ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome; follow the host's lead rather than assuming a universal custom.

Language and dining: Ask which language your counterpart prefers. Observe table customs and ask about ingredients or dietary restrictions. Avoid treating regional or generational differences as a single national rule.

Photography: Ask before photographing people and respect restrictions at transport, government, and security-sensitive sites. Check current local rules before sharing images publicly.

preArrival.simple: Compare Kigali flights via Google Flights/Skyscanner and regional carriers such as RwandAir or Ethiopian Airlines. Check the Rwanda Directorate of Immigration visa page for nationality-specific rules.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Kigali International Airport (KGL) is the main gateway. Compare regional connections with RwandAir, Ethiopian Airlines, and other carriers; verify operating airline, baggage, and layover terms.

Entry: Rwanda's visa-on-arrival/eVisa arrangements and documentary requirements depend on nationality and trip purpose. Check the Directorate of Immigration or Irembo before departure, even if a general page suggests visa-on-arrival.

Climate and packing: Kigali's elevation moderates temperatures; rainy seasons affect road and hiking conditions. Check forecasts for parks and highlands and pack light rain protection and layers.

arrival24h.simple: Rwanda uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type C and J sockets. Kigali airport and city transport are straightforward to plan; check SIM registration and mobile-money visitor access.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type C and J sockets. Check device labels and bring a compatible adapter.

Connectivity and payments: Check local SIM registration with MTN or Airtel. Mobile Money is widely used domestically, but visitor account access and cash-in requirements vary; carry Rwandan francs (RWF) and a card backup.

Airport transfer: Kigali Airport lists passenger services; taxis and hotel transfers serve the city. Confirm pickup and fare before leaving.

mobility.simple: Kigali uses buses, moto-taxis, and app-booked rides; Tap&Go is a local bus payment option. Use regulated, helmeted motorcycle taxis and check intercity schedules.
mobility.detailed:
Kigali: City buses use Tap&Go smart-card payment on many services. Confirm where to obtain/top up the card and the current routes. Moto-taxis are common; choose a helmeted rider and agree destination/fare.

Ride-hailing: Yego and other local services may operate in Kigali; coverage outside the capital is limited. Confirm driver, vehicle, and fare in the app.

Intercity and walking: Coaches connect major towns; confirm departure terminal and timetable. Kigali's hills make walking routes longer than they appear; plan for elevation and rain.

dailyLiving.simple: Vuba Vuba and local listings cover some Kigali delivery addresses; verify coverage. Ask your accommodation about water and pharmacy access before rural travel.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Vuba Vuba and restaurant-specific services may be available in Kigali; check exact address, phone, and payment requirements. Expect limited coverage outside the capital.

Health and water: Ask locally about tap-water advice; use sealed or treated water if uncertain. Carry essential medication in original packaging and locate the nearest pharmacy before leaving Kigali.

Payments and food: RWF cash, cards, and mobile money are used differently by venue. Try local dishes such as brochettes and ask about ingredients. Tipping is optional and venue-dependent.

socialCode.simple: Use a polite greeting, ask before photographing people, and follow host cues at home. At memorial sites, observe posted rules and a respectful tone.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings and visits: A courteous greeting is a good default. Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome; household customs vary.

Photography and memorials: Ask permission before photographing people. Follow strict posted instructions at memorials and public institutions.

Language and dining: Kinyarwanda is widely spoken alongside English, French, and Swahili. Ask which language is preferred and about dietary needs; avoid generalizing from one social setting.

preArrival.simple: Robert L. Bradshaw (SKB) and Nevis (NEV) serve different islands; compare regional flights and ferry connections. Check St Kitts and Nevis entry rules by passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: SKB serves St Kitts; NEV has a smaller network for Nevis. Compare regional flights with ferry transfer time and operating days included.

Entry: Visa requirements depend on nationality and stay. Check St Kitts and Nevis Immigration before booking and verify onward/return document requirements.

Climate and packing: Tropical heat and storm season affect flights and ferries. Monitor official weather notices and bring sun/rain protection.

arrival24h.simple: St Kitts and Nevis uses 230 V / 60 Hz Type D/G sockets and East Caribbean dollars. Confirm SIM, airport taxi, and ferry details before landing.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 60 Hz, Type D and G sockets. Check device compatibility and adapter.

Connectivity and money: XCD is local; cards and mobile signal vary by island. Keep cash for small vendors and check roaming.

Arrival: SKB and NEV have separate taxi and transfer options. Use marked services and confirm fare; ferry terminals are separate and schedules can change.

mobility.simple: Local buses and taxis serve St Kitts/Nevis; the inter-island ferry links Basseterre and Charlestown. Confirm return schedules and last service.
mobility.detailed:
On-island: Public buses run on major roads, with route and frequency varying. Ask locally about stops and last departures; taxis are available at visitor hubs.

Between islands: Ferry service connects Basseterre and Charlestown. Confirm timetable, fare, port, and weather notices before planning a connection.

Walking: Roads can be narrow with limited sidewalks. Use caution in heat and at night; confirm safe pedestrian routes locally.

dailyLiving.simple: Restaurant delivery is limited and address-specific. Ask lodging about water, groceries, and pharmacy access before visiting Nevis or remote beaches.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery and shops: Contact businesses directly to confirm delivery area, phone, hours, and payment; app coverage is limited.

Health and water: Ask accommodation about local water advice and the nearest pharmacy. Bring essential prescriptions; stock is limited outside main towns.

Money and dining: XCD is used; USD may be accepted in tourist businesses. Check menus for allergens and the bill for service charge.

socialCode.simple: Use a courteous greeting, ask before photography, and follow host cues on shoes and gifts. Island customs vary between St Kitts and Nevis.
socialCode.detailed:
Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome.

Public settings: English is official. Ask permission before photographing people or private property.

Inter-island: Follow local rules at beaches, churches, and community events; customs differ by household.

preArrival.simple: Hewanorra (UVF) serves the south; George F. L. Charles (SLU) serves Castries. Compare flights with the full island transfer included and check entry rules by passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: UVF is the main international gateway; SLU serves regional flights near Castries. Select airport based on lodging region and transfer time.

Entry: Saint Lucia's visa and stay rules depend on nationality and trip details. Check Immigration or the government portal before booking.

Climate and packing: Tropical heat, rain, and storm season affect ferry/road plans. Check forecasts and pack rain/sun protection and hiking shoes.

sources.topic: Saint Lucia Air and Sea Ports Authority

arrival24h.simple: Saint Lucia uses 240 V / 50 Hz Type G sockets and East Caribbean dollars. Check which airport you arrive at and arrange a taxi/shuttle to your region.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 240 V / 50 Hz, Type G sockets. Check appliance input before use.

Connectivity and money: XCD is local; USD may be accepted in tourist businesses. Confirm SIM/roaming and card acceptance outside Castries.

Airport transfer: UVF and SLU serve different coasts and are not interchangeable. Use authorized taxi dispatch or hotel transfer; confirm fare and route.

mobility.simple: Minibuses and taxis connect towns; there is no rail/metro. Road travel is winding, so plan extra time between airports, resorts, and trailheads.
mobility.detailed:

Airport transfer: Bratislava Airport publishes current bus and shuttle links, including connections to the city and Vienna. Check the timetable, stop, and ticket with the operator on travel day. Use official taxi pickup or a verified booking and confirm the fare.

mobility.simple: Bratislava uses buses, trams, and trolleybuses; IDS BK covers regional transport. Check current DPB and Slovak Rail (ZSSK) routes and tickets.

Ride-hailing and walking: App availability varies by city; use licensed providers and verify the pickup point. Historic centers may have cobbles and restricted vehicle access, so allow time on foot.

preArrival.simple: Compare Johannesburg, Cape Town, and Durban gateways with Google Flights/Skyscanner; check FlySafair or Airlink directly for domestic routes. Visa requirements depend on passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: O.R. Tambo (JNB), Cape Town (CPT), and King Shaka (DUR) serve different regions. Use broad flight search, then compare FlySafair, Airlink, and full-service carriers directly for domestic legs and baggage.

Entry: South African visa and eVisa eligibility depends on nationality, purpose, and port of entry. Check the Department of Home Affairs and your nearest mission before booking; do not rely on an airline or OTA summary.

Climate and packing: Seasons are opposite the Northern Hemisphere; coastal, inland, and highveld weather differ. Check regional forecasts and pack sun protection, layers, and rain gear.

sources.topic: South Africa Department of Home Affairs

arrival24h.simple: South Africa uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type D, M, and N sockets; Type N is increasingly common. Check load-shedding notices, roaming, and airport transfers.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz; Type D, M, and N sockets are reported, with socket availability varying by building. Check device labels and bring compatible adapters.

Connectivity and payments: Check SIM/eSIM registration and roaming. Cards are widely accepted in urban retail, but retain a backup payment method. Power interruptions can affect networks and card terminals; monitor official electricity notices.

Airport transfer: ACSA publishes passenger and airport information. Gautrain serves parts of the Johannesburg airport corridor; Cape Town and Durban use different bus/taxi options. Use official pickup points and verify schedules.

mobility.simple: Major cities have distinct systems: Gautrain, MyCiTi, Rea Vaya, and municipal buses. Minibus taxis are widely used but routes and boarding conventions are local.
mobility.detailed:
Formal transit: Gautrain links parts of Gauteng; Cape Town's MyCiTi and Johannesburg's Rea Vaya operate city corridors. Check each system's route, fare card, hours, and service alerts.

Shared travel: Minibus taxis cover many routes but use local hand signals and informal stops; ask a trusted local or choose a licensed alternative if unfamiliar. Intercity coach operators require advance station checks.

Ride-hailing and walking: Uber and Bolt are available in many cities. Confirm vehicle and driver in-app and use well-lit pickup areas. Walking conditions vary substantially by district; plan routes with local advice.

dailyLiving.simple: Checkers Sixty60, Mr D, and Uber Eats are useful urban examples; availability varies by postcode. Follow municipal water and power notices at your exact stay.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery and shopping: Checkers Sixty60, Mr D, and Uber Eats operate in covered zones; enter the exact address to confirm service and payment options. Grocery delivery is much less available outside larger urban areas.

Water and health: Water advisories are local and can change. Check the municipality and accommodation for current tap-water guidance. Pharmacies are common in cities, but carry prescriptions in original packaging and check import rules.

Food and alcohol: Retail hours and alcohol rules vary by province and municipality. Check posted rules and receipts; tipping depends on service and whether a charge is included.

socialCode.simple: South Africa is multilingual and regionally diverse. Ask before photographing people; follow host cues on greetings, home customs, and language preference.
socialCode.detailed:
Language and introductions: South Africa has multiple official languages and local preferences. Ask which language a person prefers; a respectful greeting is better than assuming one norm.

Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small gift is welcome. Dining customs differ across households; check dietary needs and follow the host's lead.

Photography and safety: Ask permission before photographing people or private property. Follow site rules and local safety guidance, especially at remote or wildlife locations.

preArrival.simple: Compare Seoul (ICN/GMP), Busan, and regional gateways with Google Flights/Skyscanner; check Korean e-visa/K-ETA rules by passport and travel date.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Incheon (ICN) is the main long-haul gateway; Gimpo (GMP) serves domestic/regional flights, with Busan (PUS) useful for the southeast. Compare broad search with Korean Air, Asiana, and low-cost carriers; verify airport and baggage.

Entry: Visa-free status, K-ETA, and e-visa requirements vary by passport and may change. Check Korea Visa Portal and the official K-ETA site before departure; don't infer eligibility from a booking website.

Climate and packing: Seoul has cold winters, hot humid summers, and seasonal air-quality issues. Check forecasts and PM2.5 alerts; pack layers and rain protection.

arrival24h.simple: South Korea uses 220 V / 60 Hz Type C and F sockets. T-money is widely useful; prepare Naver/Kakao Maps and verify visitor SIM/eSIM options.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 60 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check device voltage and bring a compatible adapter.

Connectivity and payments: Tourist SIM/eSIMs are available from carriers and airport vendors; confirm ID requirements. T-money helps with transit. Foreign cards work at many businesses, but local wallet onboarding can require a Korean number/account.

Airport transfer: Incheon Airport has AREX, bus, and taxi options; Gimpo is separate. Check official airport route/timetable and terminal before choosing a connection.

mobility.simple: Seoul has metro, buses, and rail; use T-money and current operator apps. Kakao T is a common taxi app, while Naver/Kakao Maps often outperform Google Maps for local routing.
mobility.detailed:
Seoul: Metro and buses have extensive coverage. Use T-money and check transfer/tap-out rules; live route and disruption information is available from local operators.

Navigation and taxis: Naver Map or Kakao Map provide local routing. Kakao T can book taxis, but account/payment setup may require a Korean phone number or card; verify before relying on it.

Intercity: KTX and other trains connect major cities; book through official Korail and confirm station and train type. Sidewalks are generally organized in central areas but can be crowded.

dailyLiving.simple: Baemin and Coupang Eats are common delivery apps, but foreign signup/payment may be difficult. Tap water is treated; check building-specific notices and pharmacy rules.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Baemin and Coupang Eats dominate many urban areas. Korean phone number, local address format, and payment setup may be required; check access before depending on delivery.

Health and water: Municipal tap water is treated; follow local advisories and accommodation guidance. Pharmacies can advise on common medicines, but bring prescriptions in original packaging and verify import rules.

Payments and food: Cards and contactless are common, though some small businesses prefer local wallets. Ask about spice, allergens, and ingredients; check venue-specific buffet terms.

socialCode.simple: Use two hands when offering/receiving items in formal settings; remove shoes where household or venue rules require. Ask before photos and follow temple signage.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings and etiquette: A small bow or polite verbal greeting is appropriate; formality varies by age and setting. Two-handed exchanges are courteous in formal situations.

Home and dining: Remove shoes where requested. Wait for the host or senior diner to begin in formal meals; ask about dietary restrictions.

Photography: Ask before photographing people, homes, or ceremonies. Follow rules at temples and memorials; avoid broad assumptions about individual preferences.

preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Madrid (MAD), Barcelona (BCN), Málaga (AGP), and island airports serve different regions. Compare broad flight search with AZair for low-cost European legs, then verify airport, baggage, and schedule with the airline.

Entry rules: Spain is in Schengen. Visa eligibility depends on nationality and time already spent in the area; check current European Commission rules and Spanish consular guidance.

Climate and packing: Northern Atlantic, central plateau, Mediterranean coast, and Canary Islands have different conditions. Check forecasts for the actual region and season; pack sun/rain protection and suitable walking shoes.

arrival24h.simple: Spain uses 230 V / 50 Hz Type F sockets and the euro. Aena lists airport transfers; check the exact city and terminal before choosing rail, bus, or taxi.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 230 V / 50 Hz, Type F sockets. Check device voltage and adapter fit.

Connectivity and payment: Euro, cards, and contactless are common. Check roaming/eSIM terms; keep a small cash backup for occasional exceptions.

Airport transfer: Aena operates airports across Spain with city-specific rail, bus, and taxi connections. Check the airport's official transport page, terminal, and first/last service before arrival.

sources.topic: Aena airport access and passenger information

mobility.simple: Madrid, Barcelona, and other cities have distinct metro/tram/bus systems. Renfe serves national rail; check regional operator tickets and current service notices.
mobility.detailed:
City transit: Madrid and Barcelona have metro, bus, and commuter rail; tickets and passes are city-specific. Check Metro de Madrid, TMB, or the local operator for routes, fares, and service changes.

Intercity: Renfe operates national rail services, alongside regional operators. Confirm station, train type, reservation, and disruptions before travel.

Ride-hailing and walking: Uber, Cabify, or Bolt coverage varies by city and regulation. Historic centres can restrict cars and have cobbled streets; check pickup zones and walkability.

dailyLiving.simple: Glovo, Just Eat, and Uber Eats operate in many cities; verify postcode coverage. Tap-water and pharmacy guidance are local, especially on islands and in rural areas.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Glovo, Just Eat, and Uber Eats are city/address-dependent. Check phone, payment, and opening hours in-app before relying on delivery outside major centres.

Health and water: Municipal tap-water supplies are generally treated, but follow local notices and ask accommodation about building-specific issues. Check the duty-pharmacy rota and bring prescribed medicines in original packaging.

Food and payment: Meal timing and service customs vary by region and venue. Ask about ingredients/allergens, check the bill for service charges, and tip at your discretion.

socialCode.simple: At churches, follow posted dress and photography rules. Greetings and meal timing vary by region; ask before photos and follow your host's lead at home.
socialCode.detailed:
Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Household customs vary; don't assume shoes are always removed or kept on.

Religious and public sites: Follow posted rules on clothing, photography, and access. Ask permission before photographing people or private property.

Interaction: Spanish is the national language, with co-official regional languages in some areas. Ask which language is preferred and use a polite greeting; avoid generalizing one region's customs to the country.

preArrival.simple: For Southeast Asia, compare AirAsia MOVE and Traveloka with Google Flights/Skyscanner; Scoot is an airline, not a search engine. Check Thailand e-Visa eligibility by passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight search and routing: Bangkok (BKK/DMK) is the main hub; Chiang Mai, Phuket, and other cities serve regional trips. AirAsia MOVE and Traveloka are regional booking platforms; Scoot is a carrier. Compare with Google Flights/Skyscanner, then check baggage and airport with the airline.

Entry: Thailand's e-Visa application is online, but eligibility and required documents depend on nationality and current policy. Use the official Thai e-Visa portal and the relevant embassy; do not assume visa-on-arrival or visa-free access.

Climate and packing: Hot/humid conditions year-round, with regional monsoon and cooler northern-season variation. Check forecasts, heat and air-quality alerts; pack rain protection and modest temple clothing.

arrival24h.simple: Thailand uses 220 V / 50 Hz with Type A, B, C, F, and O sockets; bring a compatible adapter. PromptPay is domestic infrastructure, not guaranteed for visitors.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 50 Hz; Type A, B, C, F, and O socket patterns are reported. Check your accommodation and device labels; an adapter does not convert voltage.

Connectivity and payments: Buy a SIM/eSIM through a recognized provider and check registration requirements. PromptPay QR is common domestically, but visitors may not be able to link it; keep THB cash and an international card.

Airport transfers: Bangkok BKK and DMK have separate rail, bus, and taxi options. Check Airports of Thailand and the airport's current transport page; use marked taxi queues or official app pickup zones.

mobility.simple: Bangkok combines BTS, MRT, buses, and boats; Rabbit and stored-value products are not universally interchangeable. Grab, Bolt, and local motorcycle taxis cover many urban areas.
mobility.detailed:
Bangkok: BTS, MRT, Airport Rail Link, river boats, and buses use distinct operators and ticket rules. Check current routes and which cards/payment methods are accepted before transferring.

Ride-hailing: Grab and Bolt are available in many cities; use the app pickup point and check vehicle/plate. Motorcycle taxis are useful for short trips but helmets and road conditions matter.

Intercity: Trains, coaches, and domestic flights connect regions. Book through the official operator or recognized provider and verify station/airport, especially for overnight services.

dailyLiving.simple: LINE MAN and GrabFood serve many urban areas; check exact-address coverage. Water, pharmacy, alcohol-sale hours, and payment access vary by location and rules.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery and shopping: LINE MAN and GrabFood are common city examples; confirm address, phone, cash/card options, and operating hours in-app. 7-Eleven is widespread but not every branch stocks the same products.

Water and pharmacy: Use sealed or reliably filtered water unless your accommodation confirms local guidance. Pharmacies are common in cities; check prescription rules for medicines you bring.

Food and payment: Ask about spice, fish sauce, allergens, and dietary needs. Alcohol sales are subject to Thai law and local restrictions; check current rules and posted hours rather than relying on old summaries.

socialCode.simple: At temples, cover shoulders and knees and remove shoes where directed. Avoid touching people's heads or pointing feet at sacred images; ask before photos.
socialCode.detailed:
Temples: Follow posted dress rules, remove shoes where instructed, and observe signs restricting photography or access. Keep feet pointed away from Buddha images and altars.

Greetings and public conduct: A wai may be appropriate, but context varies; a polite verbal greeting is also fine. Keep interactions respectful and avoid confrontations in public.

Home visits: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Customs differ by household; follow the host's lead.

preArrival.simple: Piarco (POS) serves Trinidad; ANR serves Tobago. Compare Caribbean Airlines and regional connections with Google Flights/Skyscanner; check entry rules by passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: POS is the main international hub; ANR serves Tobago. Compare fare plus inter-island flight/ferry costs and confirm the terminal and baggage with the carrier.

Entry: Visa and stay rules depend on nationality, purpose, and route. Check Trinidad and Tobago Immigration before purchase.

Climate and packing: Tropical climate and rainy season can affect flights/ferries. Check weather advisories; pack sun/rain protection and light layers.

sources.topic: Airports Authority of Trinidad and Tobago

arrival24h.simple: Trinidad and Tobago uses 115 V / 60 Hz Type A/B sockets; TTD is local currency. Check POS/ANR transfer options and mobile-wallet/card terms.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 115 V / 60 Hz, Type A and B sockets. Check device voltage and adapter fit.

Connectivity and money: TTD is local; card acceptance is common in many businesses but carry cash for taxis/small vendors. Confirm SIM, roaming, ATM fees, and Mobile Money access.

Airport transfer: POS and ANR have separate ground transport; check the airport's current taxi/bus service. The inter-island ferry uses a separate Port of Spain terminal; verify transfer time.

mobility.simple: Port of Spain uses PTSC buses, maxi-taxis, and route taxis; ferries and domestic flights connect Tobago. Routes and fares are local—confirm before boarding.
mobility.detailed:
Public transport: PTSC buses and privately operated maxi-taxis serve major routes. Confirm route, stop, fare, and operating hours locally.

Between islands: The Port of Spain–Scarborough ferry and domestic flights connect Trinidad and Tobago. Check current operator schedules and weather notices.

Ride-hailing and walking: App service availability varies; use official pickup points and verify driver/vehicle. Sidewalks and crossings vary by district.

sources.topic: Airports Authority of Trinidad and Tobago

dailyLiving.simple: FoodDrop, restaurants, and local grocery services are address-dependent. Ask about water advisories and pharmacy opening hours for your area.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: FoodDrop and restaurant-direct services may serve Port of Spain and larger towns; confirm exact address, payment, and hours.

Health and water: Follow WASA water notices and accommodation guidance. Use bottled water if uncertain; check the local pharmacy rota and carry essential medicines.

Payments and food: TTD, cards, and local mobile wallets are used differently by business. Ask about ingredients and allergens; check the receipt for service charge.

sources.topic: Water and Sewerage Authority Trinidad and Tobago

socialCode.simple: Trinidad and Tobago is culturally diverse; ask before photos and follow host cues on greetings, gifts, and shoes. Follow event and religious-site guidance.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings and language: English is official, with local Creole widely spoken. A courteous greeting is a good start; ask which language is preferred.

Home visits: Ask about footwear and whether a small food gift is welcome. Customs vary by household and religious practice.

Photography: Ask before photographing people, homes, or religious events. Observe local event, beach, and heritage-site rules.

preArrival.simple: Compare Istanbul and regional airports with Google Flights/Skyscanner; use AZair for low-cost European connections and check Pegasus/Turkish Airlines directly. Use Turkey's official e-Visa portal only if eligible.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Istanbul (IST/SAW), Ankara (ESB), Izmir (ADB), and Antalya (AYT) serve different regions. Compare broad search engines and AZair for low-cost European legs; confirm baggage, airport, and route with Turkish Airlines, Pegasus, or the operating carrier.

Entry rules: Turkey's e-Visa eligibility is nationality- and passport-specific and may include conditions. Check the official e-Visa portal and Turkish MFA guidance; do not assume visa-on-arrival or universal e-Visa access.

Climate and clothing: Turkey spans several climate zones. Check city-specific forecasts. At mosques, follow posted dress guidance; lightweight layers and sun protection are useful in warmer seasons.

arrival24h.simple: Turkey uses lira (TRY) and 220 V / 50 Hz Type C/F sockets. IST and SAW have separate airport-transfer networks; check official airport notices and current fares.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check device voltage before use.

Connectivity and payment: The lira (TRY) is the currency. Cards are accepted widely in urban areas, but cash is useful for smaller purchases. Check roaming/eSIM and foreign-card terms with your providers.

Airport transfer: Istanbul Airport (IST) and Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) are on different sides of the city and use different connections. Check the relevant airport's current metro, bus, and taxi information; allow for traffic and verify fares before travel.

mobility.simple: Istanbul combines metro, tram, Marmaray, ferry, and bus; use Istanbulkart and Metro Istanbul's current network notices. Dolmuş routes and payment vary locally.
mobility.detailed:
Istanbul: Metro Istanbul operates rail lines; ferries, trams, and buses use separate operator information. Istanbulkart is widely used for integrated transit; check current fares, transfers, and service changes.

Other cities: Ankara and Izmir have their own metro/rail and bus operators. Check the municipal app or transport website for each city rather than assuming Istanbul's fare card works nationwide.

Shared and app-based trips: Dolmuş shared minibuses serve fixed corridors, but stops and payment practices vary. BiTaksi and Uber may dispatch licensed taxis; confirm the vehicle, route, and fare. Hills and crowded sidewalks affect walking in many districts.

sources.topic: Metro Istanbul network and service information

dailyLiving.simple: Yemeksepeti and Getir are useful urban delivery examples; coverage and payment depend on the exact address. Ask locally about tap water and pharmacy access.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Yemeksepeti, Getir, and Trendyol Go operate in parts of Turkey; service areas and operating companies can change. Check address, phone, payment, and hours in the current app before relying on it.

Health and water: Tap-water taste and local advice vary; ask your accommodation and use sealed water if uncertain. Pharmacies (eczane) have posted duty rotations; bring prescriptions in original packaging and check import rules.

Food and payment: Try regional cuisine and ask about ingredients or allergens. Alcohol sales and service hours are regulated and can vary by locality. Check the bill for service charges; tipping is discretionary.

socialCode.simple: At mosques, follow posted clothing and shoe-removal rules. Ask before photographing people; for home visits, check whether a small gift is welcome.
socialCode.detailed:
Religious sites: Follow posted guidance on clothing, footwear, prayer areas, and photography. Carry a scarf or covering if you plan to visit a mosque.

Home visits and dining: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food or tea gift is appropriate. Alcohol is not a suitable default gift; check the host's preferences.

Greetings and conduct: Customs vary by region and individual. Begin politely, let the other person set the greeting style, and ask permission before photographing people or private property.

preArrival.simple: Compare Entebbe (EBB) routes with Google Flights/Skyscanner and Uganda Airlines or regional carriers. Uganda's e-visa system is official; check eligibility before booking.
preArrival.detailed:
Flight routing: Entebbe (EBB) is the main international gateway for Kampala. Compare Google Flights/Skyscanner with Uganda Airlines and regional operators; verify baggage, transfers, and schedules directly.

Entry: Uganda uses an official electronic visa/permit system. Requirements depend on nationality, purpose, and route; apply through visas.immigration.go.ug and check current notices.

Climate and packing: Equatorial conditions are moderated by elevation; rain patterns and conditions differ by region. Check park/road forecasts and pack rain layers, sun protection, and suitable footwear.

arrival24h.simple: Uganda uses 240 V / 50 Hz Type G sockets. MTN/Airtel SIM and Mobile Money access require local registration; carry UGX cash and confirm airport transfer.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 240 V / 50 Hz, Type G sockets. Check device voltage and bring a compatible adapter.

Connectivity and payments: Local SIM registration is required. MTN MoMo and Airtel Money are common domestic rails, but visitor account access varies; keep Ugandan shillings (UGX) and a card backup.

Airport transfer: Entebbe Airport is outside central Kampala. Arrange a hotel transfer, licensed taxi, or verified app trip in advance and confirm fare, especially for late arrivals.

mobility.simple: Kampala uses matatus, buses, and boda-bodas; SafeBoda and ride-hailing operate in parts of the city. Check route and safety conditions before each trip.
mobility.detailed:
Kampala: Shared taxis (matatus) and buses run on busy corridors; stops and fares require local knowledge. Ask your accommodation or use a vetted route source.

Boda-bodas and apps: SafeBoda, Uber, or other apps may be available by district. Choose a helmeted, identifiable rider; confirm route and fare in-app and consider traffic/weather.

Intercity: Coaches serve major towns and park destinations. Confirm the operator, departure terminal, and daylight arrival options; road conditions and travel times vary.

dailyLiving.simple: Glovo and local delivery services reach parts of Kampala; verify address and payment. Use bottled or treated water and confirm pharmacy access before park trips.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Glovo and local services may cover Kampala addresses; check exact zone, phone, payment, and hours. Coverage outside the capital is limited.

Health and water: Use sealed/treated water unless local advice confirms safety. Pharmacies and clinics are less available near remote parks; carry essential medicines in original packaging and verify import rules.

Payments and food: UGX cash is useful; mobile-money registration depends on local SIM and ID rules. Ask about ingredients and allergens; check the bill for service charges.

socialCode.simple: Ask before photographing people or cultural events. At a home visit, ask about footwear and gifts; customs vary among Uganda's many communities.
socialCode.detailed:
Greetings and language: English and Swahili are official languages, with many local languages in daily use. Ask which language is comfortable and use a respectful greeting.

Home and dining: Ask whether to remove shoes and whether a small food gift is welcome. Follow the host's lead and ask about dietary needs.

Photography: Seek permission before photographing people, ceremonies, or private property. Follow park, border, and security-site restrictions.

preArrival.simple: Do not assume commercial flights are operating to your destination. Check current government travel advice and Ukrainian transport updates; entry rules depend on your passport.
preArrival.detailed:
Route planning: Security conditions and aviation operations can change. Do not rely on Google Flights, Skyscanner, or an old itinerary alone; confirm current airspace and carrier operations through official sources and follow your government's travel advice. Ukrzaliznytsia publishes official rail information and booking links; cross-border routes and connections can change at short notice.

Entry rules: Visa requirements depend on nationality, purpose, and stay. Check Ukraine's MFA guidance and the relevant embassy before departure.

Climate and packing: Conditions vary from the Black Sea coast to the Carpathians. Check the forecast for every region and season; use layers, rain protection, and sturdy footwear.

arrival24h.simple: Ukraine uses 220 V / 50 Hz Type C and F sockets. Power and mobile service can be interrupted; carry a charged power bank and check current local alerts.
arrival24h.detailed:
Power: 220 V / 50 Hz, Type C and F sockets. Check your device label and adapter before use. Electricity availability can change with local conditions; keep essential devices charged when possible.

Connectivity and payments: Check roaming or eSIM coverage with your provider. Keep offline maps and important addresses; service can be interrupted. The local currency is the hryvnia (UAH). Cards are common in cities, but keep some cash for outages or small purchases.

Arrival and onward travel: Confirm the operating status of the airport and border crossing before travel. For rail, use official Ukrzaliznytsia schedules and booking links. Follow official alerts and instructions at stations.

mobility.simple: Use current official city-transit and Ukrzaliznytsia updates. Service may change with security alerts; follow local air-raid instructions and shelter guidance.
mobility.detailed:
Kyiv and other cities: Metro, bus, tram, and trolleybus services operate by municipality; check the local operator's current service notices, hours, and ticketing. Air-raid alerts can interrupt service or change access; follow official instructions and know the nearest shelter.

Intercity: Ukrzaliznytsia is the primary official rail source. Confirm schedules, station changes, and boarding details on the day of travel.

Taxis and walking: Check current availability of licensed taxi apps at your location and confirm the pickup point. Avoid photographing transport, military, or infrastructure sites where restricted; use marked crossings and follow local security notices.

dailyLiving.simple: Glovo and grocery delivery cover some Ukrainian cities; check your exact address. Follow local notices for water, electricity, pharmacy hours, and payment access.
dailyLiving.detailed:
Delivery: Check Glovo or local listings at the exact address; coverage and operating hours vary by city and can change with local conditions. Confirm phone-number, payment, and delivery instructions in the app.

Pharmacy and water: Ask your accommodation about current local water guidance and open pharmacies. Bring necessary medicines in original packaging and verify import rules. Keep essential supplies for possible service interruptions.

Payments and food: Use Ukrainian hryvnia (UAH); card and mobile payment availability may be affected by power or network interruptions. Check receipts for service charges and ask about ingredients or dietary needs.

socialCode.simple: Ask which language a person prefers; do not assume Ukrainian and Russian are interchangeable. Follow air-raid, photography, and security instructions without exception.
socialCode.detailed:
Language and introductions: Ukrainian is the state language, and language preferences vary by person and region. Ask politely which language your counterpart prefers; do not assume that Ukrainian and Russian are interchangeable.

Home and hospitality: Ask about footwear and gift preferences when visiting. A small food gift can be appropriate, but follow the host's lead and ask about dietary needs.

Security and photography: Follow air-raid alerts, shelter instructions, and restrictions on photographing people, transport, military activity, or infrastructure. Do not publish location-sensitive images. Customs differ by household; avoid national-character generalizations.
